CHG:4.87.0.full: The Industry Landscape shows which post-quantum mechanism replaces which classical one, search results stop mixing crosswalk rows into the compliance frameworks, the site stays up for visitors in the minutes after a release, search engines can index every page, and a night of evidence work re-addresses 51 organisation sources and prunes copies that were never the cited document.
CHG:4.87.0.release_notes:
The Industry Landscape shows which post-quantum mechanism replaces which classical one, search results stop mixing crosswalk rows into the compliance frameworks, the site stays up for visitors in the minutes after a release, search engines can index every page, and a night of evidence work re-addresses 51 organisation sources and prunes copies that were never the cited document.

### Added

- **The Industry Landscape now says which post-quantum mechanism replaces which classical one**: RSA is split into its signature and key-exchange roles, every PQC family names what it replaces, each tile pairs mechanisms by kind instead of listing "Classical" beside "PQC", and every row links to the Learn module that teaches it. Four badge contradictions fixed (rows that showed "PQC in production" with no PQC mechanism, or "in production" beside "standardising").

### Fixed

- **Search results no longer show crosswalk rows as compliance frameworks**: the search index had read 752 candidate crosswalk rows as frameworks since 09-17 (131 duplicate entries); the index is rebuilt with the 184 real frameworks.
- **The site keeps working for visitors during the minutes after a release**: a visitor who loaded the previous release could hit a blank page when its files were replaced; the previous release's boot files are now kept across a deploy, and the app retries once before showing an error.
- **Search engines can index every page**: sitemap and canonical addresses no longer redirect, the Navigate page is now prerendered and listed, and each page's last-modified date is real instead of a constant.

### Data

- **51 organisation sources re-addressed after a web-search pass**: 25 Sources-directory and 26 trusted-sources rows that pointed at a dead or blocked address now point at a page the evidence door verified as the organisation's own; 145 could not be found and stay marked.
- **250 registry concepts whose source row had been deprecated are resolved**: 68 remapped to the active successor, 18 resolved through their table, 165 deprecated with their source's own reason, with the crosswalks that cite them following; 280 verbatim crosswalk candidates merged at low confidence.
- **Every glossary term now links to a Learn module that actually uses it**: 61 unlinked terms assigned (38 by whole-word use in the module's own text, 23 by their definitions).
- **20 leader references added and 9 ANSSI certification reports re-addressed**: 18 new library documents back leaders who cited nothing; 9 ANSSI reports whose cyber.gouv.fr addresses are dead now point at the Common Criteria portal copy, verified; 16 CMVP records lose a "Security Policy Not Available" placeholder that had been counted as a document.
- **Copies that were never the cited document no longer back a row**: 15 paid ISO standards drop a local copy that was the publisher's paywall page, two vendor roadmap captures are re-filed in their real format, one African Union convention scan is now readable text, and two library dates (PCI DSS quick reference, CNSSP 15) now match the document they cite.

CHG:4.88.0.full: Every page reads better for screen-reader and keyboard users, the learning paths and role boards reach more of the site, and the Crypto Lab opens on a different set of tools for each role.
CHG:4.88.0.release_notes:
Every page reads better for screen-reader and keyboard users, the learning paths and role boards reach more of the site, and the Crypto Lab opens on a different set of tools for each role.

### Added

- **Every role board now opens a Learn module**: the executive, GRC, architect and researcher home boards had no card pointing at a learning module at all; nine "why this matters" cards now open the module on that role's own learning path that makes the same argument (governance, risk register, migration programme, deadlines, testing evidence, standards bodies, quantum threats, verification and closure).
- **The Crypto Lab "Start here" picks differ by role**: developers, architects and researchers used to see the same three HSM tools; each role now gets three tools chosen for it (17 distinct tools across the seven roles instead of 12), and the flagship tool leads each category rail.
- **A module lists every Playground tool built for it**: modules with several hands-on tools (Entropy & Randomness has five, PKI has three) offered only one; the others now appear in an "Also in the Playground" row at the end of the module. The TPM 2.0 playground gained a home module (Secure Boot).
- **Researchers can browse 43 more modules by algorithm and standard**: every module now carries the algorithms and standards its own references declare, so the algorithm/standard filter on the Learn page and the "Related modules" panel cover all 65 modules instead of 22. Twenty standards join the filter (NIST IR 8547, CNSA 2.0, FIPS 140-3, NIST CSWP 39, EO 14306 and others).
- **Five guided workshops now run on a phone**: Compliance Strategy, Verification & Closure, PQC Business Case, Crypto Registry and CBOM open their real workshop inside the mobile module view behind a Learn / Workshop switch, instead of asking you to switch to a laptop. Every step was checked at phone width first; workshops that need a wider screen keep the notice.
- **SOC detection and automotive modules reach the roles that need them**: SOC Implementation for PQC joins the architect and GRC paths, Automotive PQC joins the architect and ops paths — both were on one path only.

### Fixed

- **Small labels are readable again on 40 pages**: level badges, "(NIST L1)" tags, track chips and status labels sat below the WCAG contrast floor (some at 1.2:1) because they were dimmed with opacity or used the brand tint as text; text now uses the legible variant of each colour and the dimming is gone. Achievement toasts slide instead of fading, so they no longer flash unreadable text while dismissing.
- **Every page has a level-one heading, on desktop and on the phone**: 45 pages (all 37 business tools among them) had none, and no page had one in the mobile layout; assistive technology can now jump to the page title everywhere.
- **Wide tables can be scrolled with the keyboard**: tables and code blocks that overflow now receive keyboard focus only while they actually overflow, so keyboard users can scroll them and nobody gets empty tab stops when they fit.
- **Links inside paragraphs are underlined**: in-text links relied on colour alone (under 3:1 against the surrounding text); they are underlined now, while navigation and cards keep their styling.
- **Opening /embed directly shows a plain explanation instead of an error**: the embed address is only meaningful inside a partner site; opened on its own it used to crash to "Something went wrong".
- **Six country flags on the community directory were missing**: Sweden, Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Russia and Portugal showed a broken image.
- **The VPN and SSH comparison panels use valid list markup and the HSM learn tabs are a proper tab list**: screen readers announce them correctly.

CHG:4.9.0.full: A business-case and report release: PQC cost models get an honest rebuild with a new side-by-side comparison tool, the exec-tour's financial docs are now generated from that same math, and the assessment report gains discovery, vendor-risk, and program-ownership sections alongside several accuracy corrections.
CHG:4.9.0.release_notes:
A business-case and report release: PQC cost models get an honest rebuild with a new side-by-side comparison tool, the exec-tour's financial docs are now generated from that same math, and the assessment report gains discovery, vendor-risk, and program-ownership sections alongside several accuracy corrections.

### Added

- **Compare six PQC cost-estimation methods side by side**: a new Cost Model Explorer runs one scenario through parametric, bottom-up, Monte-Carlo, judgemental, analogical, and risk/ALE costing families at once, including a live seeded Monte-Carlo simulation, so you can see how far the methods diverge instead of trusting a single number.
- **A "Choosing a Costing Model" methodology guide**: explains the six cost-model families with authoritative anchors (migration timelines by organization size, Mosca's inequality, the OMB $7.1B federal estimate) and two new peer-reviewed/preprint library references.
- **Search and filter the Roadmap Builder's regulatory deadline list**: the 82-entry deadline panel now has a search box and a country filter instead of one unsorted wall of chips.
- **A program-level ownership block in the assessment report**: capture the program owner, budget owner, and accountable executive — the accountability level boards actually ask about, distinct from the per-finding "Responsible" column.
- **A cryptographic discovery / inventory section in the report**: shows your self-reported algorithms (or coarse categories if unknown) as a starting inventory, explicitly labelled "not a scan," with links to the CBOM learning module and Migrate's inventory tooling.
- **A third-party & vendor PQC risk section in the report**: lists the catalog products matched to your industry/infrastructure profile, their vendor, and that vendor's tracked PQC commitment, framed by your assessed vendor-dependency model.

### Changed

- **Exec-tour and board-deck financial figures are now generated from the same math as the real tools**: the ROI, breach-cost, cost-of-inaction, and board-pitch numbers shown in the narrated executive walkthrough are computed live from shared calculations rather than hand-authored estimates, so they can no longer drift from what you'd get running the tools yourself.
- **Breach Simulator, Cost of Inaction Analyzer, and Cost Model Explorer are now full Command Center tools**: reachable directly from the Command Center and completable as simulation steps, not just standalone workshop exercises.
- **Program Charter and Initial Scoping Assessment now match the migration framework more completely**: the charter adds purpose/objectives, scope, success criteria, and escalation triggers, offers all 8 steering-committee seats, and models a three-tier decision cadence (PMO/SteerCo/Board); scoping now captures a per-system priority tier and ownership rather than a flat list.
- **Quick assessments no longer silently upgrade to "comprehensive"**: the quick track was collecting two fields that flipped an internal completeness flag, so it was mislabelled and never showed the upgrade nudge or section locks — the quick path is now genuinely lighter, and report locks reflect the assessment mode you actually chose.
- **The report's table of contents now covers every section**: the ROI Calculator, progress-over-time, and workforce-gap sections are now reachable from both the desktop rail and mobile menu, and the mobile section-jump menu now tracks your scroll position like the desktop rail does.
- **The report's persona-aware summary appears once, at the top**: the "what this means for you" narrative previously appeared twice with two different framings; it now lives solely in the top verdict block and reflects your actual result rather than a static per-persona blurb.
- **The report footer's next-step suggestions now reflect your actual result**: previously ordered by persona alone, the suggested next step now leads with the destination your specific findings point to (e.g. Migrate for a vulnerable algorithm, the executive tools for a hard compliance deadline).

### Fixed

- **The Breach Scenario Simulator's cost model was inflated roughly 2.5–10x**: it was double-counting reputational cost and the quantum-risk multiplier, and its industry breach-cost table had drifted from the source figures; rebuilt on a single documented baseline.
- **The Cost of Inaction Analyzer's regulatory penalty never actually applied**, and quantum risk was double-counted when fed from the Breach Simulator: both calculation bugs are fixed, and "migrate now" no longer shows zero residual risk.
- **The ROI Calculator now cross-checks its estimate against an independent method**: rather than presenting one bottom-up number as certain, it reconciles it against an assessment-derived estimate and flags whether the two agree.
- **Removed a fabricated standards quote and an overstated outcome claim from the Roadmap Builder**.
- **Report's Share, Print, and Board-pack buttons now give honest feedback**: they previously could fail or succeed silently; the Download PDF button is relabelled "Print / Save as PDF" to match what it actually does.
- **The report's harvest-now-decrypt-later narrative no longer conflates your regulatory migration deadline with the separate quantum-computer arrival estimate**: the two drivers are now named distinctly wherever the deadline is shown.
- **The Framework Risk Lens panel was silently blank on every comprehensive assessment**: a scoring bug left it uncomputed on that path; now fixed.
- **An inverted-polarity bug in the organizational-readiness score could show the best-prepared organizations as highest-risk** in the QRA heatmap and framework-feasibility tile: corrected across scoring, display, and stored results.
- **The example report shown to first-time visitors used invalid data tokens and rendered as a near-empty report**: now uses valid tokens and shows a realistic example.

CHG:4.90.0.full: Every page now passes the automated accessibility check with no serious or moderate findings.

Every page, module and tool now ends with a next step, tools show what is related to them, and the Playground and Command Center put a role's own tools first.

GL:21-cfr-part-11.full:
FDA regulation establishing criteria for electronic records and electronic signatures in the pharmaceutical industry. Requires validated cryptographic controls for data integrity. Any PQC migration in pharma must maintain Part 11 compliance throughout the transition.
Category: standard

GL:3-d-secure.full:
A payment authentication protocol for card-not-present transactions. Version 2.x combines risk-based analysis with an optional cardholder challenge.
Acronym: 3DS
Category: protocol

GL:3gpp.full:
The partnership project that develops specifications for mobile telecommunications including 5G security architecture.
Acronym: 3GPP
Category: organization

GL:42-cfr-part-2.full:
US federal regulation providing additional privacy protections for substance use disorder patient records beyond HIPAA. Records protected under Part 2 carry heightened stigma risk if quantum-decrypted, as disclosure can lead to criminal prosecution, employment loss, and social ostracism.
Category: standard

GL:5g-aka.full:
5G Authentication and Key Agreement protocol, the primary authentication mechanism in 5G networks.
Category: protocol

GL:a-b-partition.full:
A firmware update strategy where an ECU maintains two complete firmware images (partition A and partition B). Updates are written to the inactive partition while the active partition continues running, enabling instant rollback on failure.
Category: concept

GL:acars.full:
Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System. A digital data link for transmitting short messages between aircraft and ground stations via VHF radio or SATCOM.
Acronym: ACARS
Category: protocol

GL:account-abstraction.full:
An Ethereum mechanism (ERC-4337) that enables smart contract wallets with arbitrary signature verification logic. ERC-4337 itself specifies no post-quantum algorithm; smart accounts can deploy custom validation code (such as prototype in-contract ML-DSA or FN-DSA verifiers) without a protocol hard fork, subject to gas cost and audit maturity.
Acronym: AA
Category: concept

GL:acme.full:
Automatic Certificate Management Environment, the protocol used by Let's Encrypt and other CAs to automate certificate issuance and renewal.
Acronym: ACME
Category: protocol

GL:active-scanning.full:
A network assessment technique that initiates real connections to target endpoints to probe which cryptographic algorithms they support. Unlike passive discovery, active scanning actively negotiates TLS/SSH/IKEv2 handshakes to discover PQC readiness.
Category: concept

GL:acvp.full:
A protocol, not a program: JSON messages over HTTPS through which a client registers an algorithm implementation's capabilities with a NIST test server, downloads the generated test vector sets, and uploads its responses for checking. NIST's servers that speak it are the ACVTS (Automated Cryptographic Validation Test System), operated for CAVP; CAVP, not ACVP, issues algorithm validation certificates, and CMVP validates whole modules to FIPS 140-3.
Acronym: Automated Cryptographic Validation Protocol
Category: protocol

GL:ads-b.full:
Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast. A surveillance system where aircraft broadcast their GPS-derived position, altitude, and velocity on 1090 MHz, receivable by ground stations and other aircraft.
Acronym: ADS-B
Category: protocol

GL:aes.full:
Advanced Encryption Standard, a symmetric block cipher with 128-, 192- or 256-bit keys. Quantum key-search costs depend on the attack model and implementation resources, not just the key-size label.
Acronym: AES
Category: algorithm

GL:aes-128-ctr.full: AES encryption in Counter mode with a 128-bit key; length-preserving ciphertext.

GL:aes-256-ctr.full: AES encryption in Counter mode with a 256-bit key; length-preserving ciphertext.

GL:aes-ccm.full:
Counter with CBC-MAC, an authenticated-encryption (AEAD) mode for AES that combines counter-mode encryption with a CBC-MAC authentication tag.
Acronym: CCM
Category: algorithm

GL:aes-gcm.full:
Galois/Counter Mode, an authenticated-encryption (AEAD) mode for AES that combines counter-mode encryption with a GHASH-based authentication tag in one pass.
Acronym: GCM
Category: algorithm

GL:agent-to-agent-authentication.full:
Mutual authentication between autonomous AI agents using cryptographic credentials, enabling secure communication, task delegation, and transaction execution without human intermediation.
Acronym: A2A
Category: protocol

GL:agentic-ai.full:
AI systems that can autonomously plan, make decisions, and take actions in the real world — including accessing services, making purchases, and communicating with other AI agents on behalf of users.
Category: concept

GL:algorithm-drift.full:
The gradual re-introduction of quantum-vulnerable algorithms into infrastructure after initial PQC migration — caused by CA fallback, operator error, or default IaC configurations. Detected via Prometheus alert rules and SIEM queries targeting classical algorithm identifiers.
Category: concept

GL:algorithmidentifier.full:
An ASN.1 SEQUENCE containing an OID that identifies a cryptographic algorithm, plus optional parameters. Appears in X.509 certificates to specify signature algorithms (signatureAlgorithm field) and public key algorithms (SubjectPublicKeyInfo.algorithm).
Category: concept

GL:alt-sig-certificate.full:
A single classical X.509 certificate with PQC key and signature embedded in X.509 extensions: SubjectAltPublicKeyInfo (2.5.29.72), AltSignatureAlgorithm (2.5.29.73), and AltSignatureValue (2.5.29.74). Informally called the "Catalyst" approach (NSA). Legacy validators ignore the unknown extensions; PQC-aware verifiers check both signatures.
Category: concept

GL:always-encrypted.full:
Microsoft SQL Server's client-side encryption feature: a client driver encrypts sensitive columns before they reach the database engine, and the encryption keys stay in an external key store rather than in the database. Without secure enclaves the engine handles only ciphertext. With secure enclaves, the client driver passes keys to a protected memory region inside the engine process, which decrypts there to allow richer queries.
Category: concept

GL:annualized-loss-expectancy.full:
A FAIR and traditional risk management metric representing the expected financial loss from a risk over a one-year period. Calculated as Annual Rate of Occurrence × Single Loss Expectancy. Used in PQC business cases to justify migration investment.
Acronym: ALE
Category: concept

GL:anssi.full:
French National Cybersecurity Agency, publishing PQC recommendations and cryptographic certifications for France and Europe.
Acronym: ANSSI
Category: organization

GL:arinc-653.full:
Avionics Application Standard Software Interface (ARINC 653). An RTOS partitioning standard that isolates safety-critical software functions in separate memory/time partitions on shared hardware.
Category: standard

GL:arm-cca.full:
ARM Confidential Compute Architecture, introducing Realms as isolated VM-like execution environments. Reduces TCB by separating the hypervisor from trusted firmware via a Realm Management Monitor.
Acronym: CCA
Category: concept

GL:arpc.full:
Authorization Response Cryptogram. A symmetric MAC generated by the issuer in response to an ARQC, proving the issuer authorized the transaction.
Acronym: ARPC
Category: protocol

GL:arqc.full:
Authorization Request Cryptogram. A symmetric MAC generated by the EMV card chip using a shared secret with the issuer, proving the card is genuine during online authorization.
Acronym: ARQC
Category: protocol

GL:ascon.full:
A lightweight authenticated encryption cipher selected by NIST as the standard for constrained environments (IoT, embedded devices). Very low resource requirements.
Category: algorithm

GL:asd.full:
Australian Signals Directorate, Australia's national cybersecurity agency. Published aggressive PQC migration timelines with a 2030 deadline for full transition — five years ahead of the US.
Acronym: ASD
Category: organization

GL:asil.full:
Automotive Safety Integrity Level, a risk classification defined by ISO 26262: ASIL A (lowest) to ASIL D (highest integrity requirements), plus QM (quality management, no safety requirement). The level comes from a hazard analysis of severity, exposure and controllability, and sets how rigorous the safety measures must be.
Acronym: ASIL
Category: standard

GL:asset-inventory.full:
A structured catalog of all data assets, cryptographic dependencies, and communication channels within an organisation. The foundation of any PQC migration programme — you cannot migrate what you cannot see.
Category: concept

GL:attestation.full:
A cryptographically signed statement vouching for the authenticity or properties of a device, key, or credential. Used in FIDO2, TPM, and digital identity systems.
Category: concept

GL:attestation-identity-key.full:
A restricted TPM 2.0 signing key used for TPM2_Quote — signing PCR values to prove system state to a remote verifier. The TPM 2.0 specification also calls such a key an Attestation Key (AK). TPM 2.0 library version 185 (March 2026) adds ML-DSA keys (TPM_ALG_MLDSA = 0x00A1) alongside RSA and ECC; it defines the ML-DSA-44, -65 and -87 parameter sets, and a TPM reports which of them it supports.
Acronym: AIK
Category: concept

GL:ausf.full:
Authentication Server Function, a 5G core network function that handles subscriber authentication using the 5G-AKA protocol and interfaces with the UDM for credential verification.
Acronym: AUSF
Category: concept

GL:autosar.full:
AUTomotive Open System ARchitecture, a standardized software architecture for automotive ECUs, with a Classic Platform and an Adaptive Platform. On the Classic Platform, software calls the Crypto Service Manager (CSM), which reaches software or hardware crypto drivers (for example an HSM or SHE) through the Crypto Interface. On the Adaptive Platform, the Cryptography functional cluster exposes the ara::crypto API, with crypto providers behind it.
Category: standard

GL:aws-lc.full:
Amazon's open-source cryptographic library, forked from BoringSSL. Specific AWS-LC FIPS module versions have FIPS 140-3 validation certificates; the validated boundary is the module version on the certificate, not the whole library. The aws-lc-rs Rust crate provides safe bindings.
Acronym: AWS-LC
Category: concept

GL:base-derivation-key.full:
The master symmetric key in the DUKPT key management scheme, stored in a payment HSM. All per-terminal and per-transaction keys are derived from it.
Acronym: BDK
Category: concept

GL:base58check.full:
A Bitcoin-specific encoding format that converts binary data to a human-readable alphanumeric string with a built-in checksum for error detection.
Category: concept

GL:batch-signing.full:
A cryptographic technique where a single digital signature covers multiple items simultaneously by signing a hash that commits to the entire set. In Merkle Tree Certificates, the CA signs the tree root once to authenticate potentially millions of certificates.
Category: concept

GL:bb84.full:
The first quantum key distribution protocol, proposed by Bennett and Brassard in 1984. Uses four quantum states in two conjugate bases to establish a shared secret key.
Category: protocol

GL:bes.full:
Bulk Electric System. The interconnected electrical generation and transmission resources subject to NERC reliability standards.
Acronym: BES
Category: concept

GL:bike.full:
Bit Flipping Key Encapsulation, a code-based KEM that was a NIST PQC Round 4 candidate. Uses quasi-cyclic moderate-density parity-check codes.
Acronym: BIKE
Category: algorithm

GL:biometric-permanence.full:
The property that distinguishes biometric data from all other credentials: once compromised, the underlying biometric characteristic cannot be changed. A quantum-decrypted fingerprint template is permanently exposed, unlike a password or certificate that can be rotated.
Category: concept

GL:biometric-template.full:
A mathematical representation of a biometric characteristic (fingerprint minutiae, iris code, facial feature vector) stored for matching. Unlike passwords, biometric templates cannot be revoked or reissued if compromised, making them the highest-priority target for Harvest Now, Decrypt Later attacks.
Category: concept

GL:bip-360.full:
Pay-to-Merkle-Root (P2MR), a draft Bitcoin soft fork that adds a new native SegWit output type (version 2, bc1z… addresses) working like Taproot with the elliptic-curve key-spend path removed. It contains no post-quantum signature of its own: its authors (Hunter Beast, Ethan Heilman and Isabel Foxen Duke) intend to offer a separate proposal for that upon further research. Earlier drafts were titled P2QRH.
Category: standard

GL:bip32.full:
Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 32, defining Hierarchical Deterministic (HD) wallets. Enables deriving an entire tree of key pairs from a single master seed.
Category: concept

GL:bip39.full:
Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 39 defines mnemonic seed phrases (12 or 24 words) used to back up and restore cryptocurrency wallets.
Category: concept

GL:bip44.full:
Bitcoin Improvement Proposal 44, defining a multi-account hierarchy for deterministic wallets using derivation paths like m/44'/0'/0'/0/0 (purpose/coin/account/change/index).
Category: standard

GL:bis.full:
Bank for International Settlements, the international financial institution that published the quantum-readiness roadmap (Paper 158) for the global financial system.
Acronym: BIS
Category: organization

GL:board-fiduciary-duty.full:
The legal obligation of corporate board members and executives to exercise due care in protecting organizational assets, including digital assets threatened by quantum computing. Failure to plan for known cryptographic risks may constitute a breach of fiduciary responsibility.
Category: concept

GL:boot-guard.full:
Intel's boot integrity technology: hardware-based verification of the initial BIOS startup code before it runs, according to a boot policy defined by the platform manufacturer. It is intended to help prevent the execution of unauthorized boot blocks.
Category: concept

GL:bouncy-castle.full:
Open-source cryptography library for Java and .NET. The Java edition works both as a JCA/JCE provider and as a standalone lightweight API.
Category: concept

GL:bsi.full:
German Federal Office for Information Security, providing PQC migration guidelines and recommendations for German government systems.
Acronym: BSI
Category: organization

GL:bsi-tr-02102.full:
German Federal Office for Information Security (BSI) Technical Guideline series on cryptographic recommendations, covering TLS, IPsec, SSH, and general algorithms.
Category: standard

GL:build-provenance.full:
A record documenting how a software artifact was built — including the source repository, build system, entry point, and build parameters — often distributed as a signed attestation. Answers the question "who built this and how?"
Category: concept

GL:byok.full:
Bring Your Own Key — a cloud encryption model where the customer provides and manages the root encryption key rather than using a key generated and managed by the cloud provider. Gives customers control over key lifecycle and access.
Acronym: BYOK
Category: concept

GL:c-encapsulatekey.full:
PKCS#11 v3.2 function for KEM encapsulation: given a recipient's public key it produces a ciphertext plus a freshly derived shared-secret key object — used for ML-KEM (FIPS 203).
Category: concept

GL:c-generatekeypair.full:
PKCS#11 function that generates an asymmetric key pair (public + private) directly inside the token, so the private key can be created non-extractable and never exists outside the HSM.
Category: concept

GL:c-wrapkey.full:
PKCS#11 function that encrypts (wraps) one key with another so it can be exported or backed up as ciphertext — e.g. AES key-wrap of a data key under a key-encryption key.
Category: concept

GL:ca-b-forum-sc-081v3.full:
CA/Browser Forum ballot (April 2025) that phases TLS certificate maximum validity from 398 days down to 200d (2026), 100d (2027), and 47d by March 2029. Forces every public-trust TLS deployment onto automated CLM.
Category: standard

GL:ca-browser-forum.full:
An industry body of Certificate Authorities and browser vendors that governs Web PKI certificate standards, including PQC certificate adoption rules.
Category: organization

GL:cacr.full:
Chinese Association for Cryptologic Research, the organization that ran China's independent PQC competition and is shaping the NGCC (Next-Generation Commercial Cryptographic) standards program.
Acronym: CACR
Category: organization

GL:can-bus.full:
Controller Area Network, the dominant in-vehicle serial bus protocol with an 8-byte (CAN 2.0) or 64-byte (CAN FD) payload per frame. CAN buses connect ECUs for powertrain, chassis, and body functions.
Acronym: CAN
Category: protocol

GL:cavp.full:
Cryptographic Algorithm Validation Program — the NIST/CCCS program that validates implementations of Approved algorithms and their components. Testing runs black-box through NIST's ACVTS, which speaks the ACVP protocol; implementations that complete it get an algorithm validation certificate on the CAVP validation list. Algorithm validation is a prerequisite of FIPS 140-3 module validation under CMVP.
Acronym: CAVP
Category: standard

GL:cbdc.full:
Central Bank Digital Currency, a digital form of fiat money issued by central banks. Requires quantum-safe cryptography for long-term trust.
Acronym: CBDC
Category: concept

GL:cbom.full:
Cryptography Bill of Materials — a structured inventory of all cryptographic assets, algorithms, keys, certificates, and protocols in use within a system or organisation. Analogous to a software BOM (SBOM) but focused on cryptographic dependencies.
Acronym: CBOM
Category: concept

GL:cbor.full:
Concise Binary Object Representation, a compact binary data serialization format (RFC 8949). Used in mdoc credentials, IoT protocols, and WebAuthn attestations.
Acronym: CBOR
Category: concept

GL:cc.full:
International standard (ISO/IEC 15408) for security-product evaluation. National schemes (BSI Germany, ANSSI France, NIAP US, the Canadian Common Criteria Scheme, etc.) oversee evaluation and certification; the CCRA lets participants recognise certificates authorised by Certificate Authorising Participants, within its scope (collaborative Protection Profiles, or EAL 1 to 2 with ALC_FLR). In the EU, the EUCC (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/482, applicable from 27 February 2025) builds on the SOG-IS mutual recognition agreement.
Acronym: Common Criteria
Category: organization

GL:ccc-digital-key.full:
A specification by the Car Connectivity Consortium (CCC) enabling smartphones to function as vehicle keys via NFC, BLE, or UWB. CCC Digital Key 3.0 uses ECDH P-256 key agreement and ECDSA P-256 certificates, both quantum-vulnerable.
Category: protocol

GL:cccs.full:
Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, Canada's technical authority on cybersecurity. Published the ITSM.40.001 PQC migration roadmap for the Government of Canada.
Acronym: CCCS
Category: organization

GL:ccpa.full:
California Consumer Privacy Act — U.S. state law, operative since 1 January 2020 and amended by the CPRA from 1 January 2023, giving California residents rights over their personal data. Section 1798.150 lets consumers sue for statutory damages when nonencrypted and nonredacted personal information is exposed because a business failed to maintain reasonable security. The statute does not mention post-quantum cryptography.
Acronym: CCPA
Category: standard

GL:ccra.full:
Common Criteria Recognition Arrangement — an arrangement under which participating countries plan to recognise Common Criteria (ISO/IEC 15408) certificates authorised by any Certificate Authorising Participant. Only Certificate Authorising Participants authorise certificates issued by their certification bodies; Certificate Consuming Participants recognise them without issuing their own. Recognition covers certificates for evaluations against a collaborative Protection Profile or at EAL 1 to 2 with ALC_FLR.
Acronym: CCRA
Category: organization

GL:cda.full:
Combined Data Authentication. The strongest EMV offline authentication method, combining dynamic RSA signature with the application cryptogram in a single operation.
Acronym: CDA
Category: protocol

GL:certificate-authority.full:
A trusted organization that issues digital certificates, verifying the identity of certificate holders.
Acronym: CA
Category: protocol

GL:certificate-bloat.full:
The significant increase in TLS certificate chain sizes caused by post-quantum signature algorithms. An ML-DSA-44 signature is 2,420 bytes compared to 64 bytes for ECDSA P-256, so a leaf-plus-intermediate ML-DSA-44 chain with its CertificateVerify signature carries about 9.9 KB of keys and signatures (more with ML-DSA-65/87 or longer chains), which can break constrained clients and slow connection setup.
Category: concept

GL:certificate-chain.full:
A linked sequence of X.509 certificates from a leaf (end-entity) certificate up through intermediates to a trusted root CA, establishing a chain of trust.
Category: concept

GL:certificate-lifecycle-management.full:
The provisioning, rotation, revocation, and retirement workflow for X.509 certificates across an enterprise. Under CA/B Forum SC-081v3, the maximum validity of publicly trusted TLS certificates falls to 47 days from March 2029, so renewal has to be automated: manual renewal across a large certificate inventory becomes impractical.
Acronym: CLM
Category: concept

GL:certificate-revocation-list.full:
A signed list published by a Certificate Authority containing the serial numbers of certificates that have been revoked before their expiration date.
Acronym: CRL
Category: protocol

GL:certificate-rotation-at-scale.full:
The operational challenge of replacing certificates across large infrastructure deployments when migrating to PQC algorithms, complicated by larger certificate sizes, new CA hierarchies, and the need to maintain backward compatibility during the transition period.
Category: concept

GL:certificate-signing-request.full:
A message sent to a Certificate Authority to request a digital certificate. Contains the public key and identity information.
Acronym: CSR
Category: protocol

GL:certificate-transparency.full:
An open framework (RFC 9162) that requires all publicly-trusted TLS certificates to be logged in publicly auditable logs, enabling detection of misissued certificates.
Acronym: CT
Category: protocol

GL:chacha20-poly1305.full:
A modern authenticated encryption with associated data (AEAD) cipher combining the ChaCha20 stream cipher with the Poly1305 authenticator. Quantum-safe at current key sizes.
Category: algorithm

GL:chameleon-certificate.full:
An individual Internet-Draft design that encodes differences between two X.509 certificates in a base certificate’s Delta Certificate Descriptor extension (OID 2.16.840.1.114027.80.6.1). Software can reconstruct the paired delta certificate. Base and delta are encoding roles, not fixed classical/PQC directions: a classical base can describe a PQC delta, or the pairing can be reversed.
Category: concept

GL:cipher-proxy.full:
A network device that transparently translates between different cipher suites on each side of a connection, enabling PQC on the external-facing side while maintaining classical TLS on internal connections.
Category: concept

GL:cipher-suite.full:
A named combination of cryptographic algorithms used together in a TLS connection — specifying the key exchange, authentication, bulk encryption, and hash algorithms.
Category: concept

GL:cisa.full:
Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, the U.S. agency coordinating PQC migration for critical infrastructure and publishing product category lists.
Acronym: CISA
Category: organization

GL:cka-extractable.full:
PKCS#11 attribute controlling whether a private or secret key may be wrapped. CKA_EXTRACTABLE=CK_FALSE prevents C_WrapKey export; CKA_SENSITIVE separately restricts reading protected key material with C_GetAttributeValue.
Category: concept

GL:cka-sensitive.full:
PKCS#11 key attribute that, when CK_TRUE, prevents a key's value from being revealed by C_GetAttributeValue — the token refuses to disclose the raw secret.
Category: concept

GL:cka-token.full:
PKCS#11 attribute marking an object as persistent on the token (CK_TRUE) versus a temporary session object (CK_FALSE) that disappears when the session closes.
Category: concept

GL:ckm-aes-kw.full:
PKCS#11 mechanism for AES Key Wrap (RFC 3394) — deterministic, authenticated wrapping of key material under an AES key-encryption key, with an integrity check value.
Category: concept

GL:ckm-ecdh1-derive.full: PKCS#11 mechanism for Diffie-Hellman key agreement; used for both P-256 and X25519.

GL:ckm-ml-kem.full: PKCS#11 mechanism for ML-KEM post-quantum key encapsulation (FIPS 203).

GL:ckm-sha3-256.full: SHA3-256 hash mechanism — 256-bit digest, post-quantum robust KDF primitive.

GL:ckm-sha3-256-hmac.full: HMAC using SHA3-256 — post-quantum robust MAC construction.

GL:ckr-ok.full: PKCS#11 return value meaning the call succeeded (0x00000000).

GL:classic-mceliece.full:
A code-based KEM with very large public keys but extremely conservative security assumptions. One of the oldest post-quantum proposals.
Category: algorithm

GL:classical-cryptography.full:
The traditional math-based encryption we use today, like RSA or ECC.
Category: concept

GL:classical-security-bits.full:
The cost of the best known classical attack on an algorithm, measured in equivalent brute-force operations — not the key length. RSA-2048 reaches only ~112 bits because the General Number Field Sieve (GNFS) factors large numbers sub-exponentially. ECC P-256 reaches ~128 bits because Pollard's rho is fully exponential, costing exactly k/2 bits where k is the key size. Under Shor's algorithm on a quantum computer, both reach 0 — all classical asymmetric algorithms are fully broken regardless of key size.
Category: concept

GL:cloud-security-alliance.full:
A nonprofit industry association publishing cloud-security best practices, distinct from Singapore's Cyber Security Agency (also abbreviated CSA — see that entry). Runs an active Quantum-Safe Security working group producing PQC migration guidance for cloud providers and customers.
Acronym: CSA
Category: organization

GL:cloud-signature-consortium-api.full:
Standard API for remote signature creation services, used by QTSPs for remote qualified electronic signatures. Version V2.2 was published in November 2025.
Acronym: CSC API
Category: concept

GL:cmp.full:
Certificate Management Protocol (RFC 4210), used for managing X.509 certificates including enrollment, updates, and revocation. PQC support via RFC 9810.
Acronym: CMP
Category: protocol

GL:cms.full:
Cryptographic Message Syntax, a standard for digitally signed, encrypted, or authenticated data. Foundation for S/MIME and code signing.
Acronym: CMS
Category: protocol

GL:cmvp.full:
Cryptographic Module Validation Program — a joint NIST and CCCS program that tests cryptographic modules against FIPS 140-3 requirements. Validated modules appear on the NIST CMVP validated-modules list with a certificate number, recording that an accredited laboratory tested that module version against FIPS 140-3 at the stated security level; the Approved algorithms inside it must first complete CAVP algorithm validation.
Acronym: CMVP
Category: organization

GL:cng.full:
Cryptography Next Generation — Microsoft's modern Windows cryptographic API, introduced in Windows Vista. Separates algorithm providers (BCrypt) from key storage providers (NCrypt) for better security isolation.
Acronym: CNG
Category: concept

GL:cnsa-1-0.full:
NSA's original Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite (2015), specifying classical algorithms — RSA-3072, ECDH/ECDSA P-384, SHA-384, AES-256 — for protecting National Security Systems.
Category: standard

GL:cnsa-2-0.full:
NSA's Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0, mandating PQC adoption timelines for national security systems.
Category: standard

GL:coap.full:
Constrained Application Protocol, a lightweight RESTful protocol designed for IoT devices. Runs over UDP with DTLS for security. RFC 7252 sets no fixed maximum message size: it advises avoiding IP fragmentation and, when the path MTU is unknown, assuming a 1,280-byte IP MTU, for which 1,152 bytes of message and 1,024 bytes of payload are good upper bounds. Larger exchanges, such as a PQC key exchange with kilobyte-sized keys or signatures, can use block-wise transfers, so the practical limit depends on the link, the adaptation layer and the handshake design rather than on one message size.
Acronym: CoAP
Category: protocol

GL:code-based-cryptography.full:
PQC algorithms based on the hardness of decoding random linear error-correcting codes. Used by Classic McEliece and HQC.
Category: concept

GL:code-signing.full:
Digitally signing software executables and scripts to verify their authenticity and integrity. PQC migration replaces RSA/ECDSA signatures with ML-DSA or SLH-DSA.
Category: concept

GL:column-level-encryption.full:
Database encryption applied to individual columns rather than the entire database or table. Allows selective protection of sensitive fields (SSN, credit card, health records) while leaving non-sensitive data unencrypted and queryable.
Acronym: CLE
Category: concept

GL:column-master-key.full:
The top-level key in SQL Server Always Encrypted that protects Column Encryption Keys (CEKs). The CMK is typically stored in Azure Key Vault, Windows Certificate Store, or an HSM — never in the database itself.
Acronym: CMK
Category: concept

GL:common-criteria.full:
An international standard (ISO/IEC 15408) for evaluating the security properties of IT products, used globally for government procurement.
Acronym: CC
Category: standard

GL:compliance-gap-analysis.full:
A systematic comparison of an organization's current cryptographic posture against regulatory requirements, identifying where PQC migration is needed to meet compliance deadlines. Evaluates frameworks like CNSA 2.0, DORA, NIS2, and sector-specific mandates across multiple jurisdictions.
Category: concept

GL:composite-certificate.full:
An X.509 certificate encoding both a classical and a PQC key/signature under a single composite OID. Both signatures must verify. Requires all relying parties to support the composite OID — legacy-incompatible.
Category: concept

GL:composite-signature.full:
A signature format that combines a post-quantum signature (e.g. ML-DSA) with a traditional signature (e.g. ECDSA or Ed25519) into one value that verifies as a unit. A well-constructed composite stays unforgeable as long as at least one component does, but what that protects against depends on which component is broken and on the attacker (classical or quantum).
Category: concept

GL:connection-coalescing.full:
An HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 optimization where a single TLS connection is reused for requests to multiple hostnames sharing the same IP address and TLS certificate, amortizing PQC handshake overhead across domains.
Category: protocol

GL:content-credentials.full:
C2PA’s signed provenance format for associating claims about a digital asset’s creation and editing history with that asset. Validation checks cryptographic integrity, asset binding and the signer’s credentials under a trust model. It does not by itself prove that an assertion is true, that media depicts a real event, or that content is human-created or suitable for training.
Acronym: C2PA
Category: standard

GL:cose.full:
The binary, CBOR-based counterpart to JOSE, used where compact encoding matters — IoT, constrained devices, WebAuthn/FIDO2 attestation.
Acronym: CBOR Object Signing and Encryption
Category: protocol

GL:cose-sign1.full:
A CBOR Object Signing and Encryption single-signer signature structure (RFC 9052), used by ISO 18013-5 mdocs to sign the Mobile Security Object.
Category: concept

GL:cosign.full:
An OCI-native container image signing tool from the Sigstore project. Signs images by attaching signatures as OCI referrers in the registry, with ECDSA P-256 as the common default. Supports keyless signing via OIDC identity binding with the Rekor transparency log. Check the current cosign release notes for any post-quantum signature support.
Category: concept

GL:cosigner-quorum.full:
A trust mechanism in Merkle Tree Certificate deployments where relying parties accept a signed subtree only after a configured set of external witnesses (cosigners) have co-signed it, preventing a compromised CA from silently issuing fraudulent certificates.
Category: concept

GL:cpc-code.full:
A Cooperative Patent Classification symbol (e.g. H04L9/0852) that categorizes a patent by subject matter. Jointly developed and maintained by the USPTO and the European Patent Office, CPC codes are hierarchical — sections (letters) subdivide into classes, subclasses, groups, and subgroups, with longer codes indicating more specific technology.
Acronym: CPC
Category: concept

GL:cpdlc.full:
Controller-Pilot Data Link Communications. A text-based ATC communication system replacing voice with structured data messages between pilots and air traffic controllers.
Acronym: CPDLC
Category: protocol

GL:cra.full:
EU regulation (2024/2847) imposing cybersecurity requirements on products with digital elements. Entered force December 2024; full obligations apply 11 December 2027 (reporting obligations from September 2026).
Acronym: Cyber Resilience Act
Category: standard

GL:credential-activation.full:
A TPM 2.0 protocol (TPM2_MakeCredential / TPM2_ActivateCredential) for delivering a credential to a specific TPM: the credential is protected so that only a TPM holding the matching EK private key, and the named attestation key, can release it. TPM 2.0 library version 185 (March 2026) extends the key encapsulation used in this protocol to ML-KEM keys, alongside RSA and ECC.
Category: protocol

GL:crqc.full:
Cryptographically Relevant Quantum Computer, a hypothetical future quantum computer powerful enough to break RSA, ECC, and other classical public-key cryptography.
Acronym: CRQC
Category: concept

GL:crypto-agility.full:
The ability of a system to quickly switch between cryptographic algorithms without major redesign, critical for adapting to PQC.
Category: concept

GL:crypto-agility-pattern.full:
A software design pattern that decouples cryptographic algorithm selection from application business logic, so that algorithms can be changed with little or no change to application code. Supports PQC migration.
Category: concept

GL:crypto-discovery.full:
The automated process of scanning an organization's systems to identify all cryptographic algorithms, keys, certificates, and protocols in use. The first step in PQC migration.
Category: concept

GL:crypto-inventory.full:
A comprehensive catalog of all cryptographic assets across an organization — including algorithms in use, key sizes, certificate types, library versions, protocol configurations, and their locations across code, infrastructure, and third-party systems.
Category: concept

GL:crypto-policy.full:
A system-wide configuration that sets the default cryptographic algorithm preferences for all supported applications and libraries. Red Hat-based systems use update-crypto-policies; Debian-based systems configure algorithm preferences via OpenSSL and GnuTLS configuration files.
Category: concept

GL:crypto-posture.full:
A continuous measure of an organization's cryptographic health — the proportion of systems using quantum-safe algorithms versus quantum-vulnerable ones. Tracked via Prometheus metrics, SIEM queries, and CBOM scans. Degrades over time as new classical-algorithm resources are provisioned without PQC config.
Category: concept

GL:cryptocoe.full:
An organisational operating model that centralises ownership of cryptography across an enterprise — answering 'who owns it?' for crypto-agility (capability) and CPM (program).
Acronym: Cryptographic Center of Excellence
Category: concept

GL:cryptographic-algorithm-self-test.full:
A conditional self-test that a FIPS 140-3 cryptographic module performs on the cryptographic functions of each approved algorithm it implements, before the algorithm's first operational use. A CAST may take the form of a known-answer test, a comparison test or a fault-detection test.
Acronym: CAST
Category: concept

GL:cryptographic-and-security-testing-la.full:
An independent, NVLAP-accredited laboratory (also written 'CST lab') that tests cryptographic modules for the CMVP. It tests a module to the FIPS 140-3 requirements for the security level and embodiment, and produces a written test report for the CMVP Validation Authorities, who review it. Vendors submit a module and its documentation to the accredited CSTL of their choice.
Acronym: CSTL
Category: concept

GL:cryptographic-boundary.full:
The explicitly defined perimeter that establishes the boundary of all components — the set of hardware, software or firmware components — of a cryptographic module. FIPS 140-3 test requirements have the tester verify that the module's block diagram indicates this boundary, and the module's security policy must define it precisely and list any hardware, software or firmware excluded from it.
Category: concept

GL:cryptographic-debt.full:
The accumulated technical risk from hardcoded algorithm choices, missing abstraction layers, and tight coupling between application logic and specific cryptographic implementations, making PQC migration more difficult and costly.
Category: concept

GL:cryptographic-exposure-window.full:
The period during which classically-encrypted data is at risk of retrospective decryption, from the time it is protected by a quantum-vulnerable algorithm until it is no longer sensitive. Migrating to PQC stops new data from entering the window, but ciphertext an adversary has already captured stays exposed once a CRQC exists. Adversaries exploiting HNDL attacks capture data now to decrypt once a CRQC is available.
Category: concept

GL:cryptographic-inventory.full:
A comprehensive catalog of all cryptographic algorithms, protocols, keys, and certificates in an organization, essential for planning PQC migration.
Category: concept

GL:cryptographic-posture-management.full:
The continuous, iterative management discipline of knowing what cryptography you have, keeping it healthy, and proving it across certificates, libraries, application software, and key material. Distinct from crypto-agility (capability) and from a CryptoCOE (operating model).
Acronym: CPM
Category: concept

GL:cryptrec.full:
Cryptography Research and Evaluation Committees, Japan's organization for evaluating and recommending cryptographic algorithms for government use.
Acronym: CRYPTREC
Category: organization

GL:csa.full:
Singapore's national cybersecurity authority. Publishes the Cybersecurity Code of Practice and PQC readiness guidance for critical-information-infrastructure operators. Note: also used for Cloud Security Alliance (separate org).
Acronym: Cyber Security Agency of Singapore
Category: organization

GL:cspn.full:
ANSSI's first-level security certification scheme for IT products. Faster and lighter than full Common Criteria; PQC products began entering CSPN catalogue in 2025.
Acronym: Certification de Sécurité de Premier Niveau
Category: standard

GL:csprng.full:
Cryptographically Secure Pseudo-Random Number Generator. A PRNG whose output is computationally indistinguishable from true randomness, suitable for cryptographic key generation.
Acronym: CSPRNG
Category: concept

GL:cswp-39.full:
NIST CSWP 39 — Considerations for Achieving Crypto Agility: Strategies and Practices (Update 1; first published December 19, 2025, updated June 29, 2026). Covers crypto agility in security protocols and in system implementations, a strategic plan for managing an organization's cryptographic risks, and an illustrative four-tier maturity model adapted from the NIST Cybersecurity Framework tiers (Partial → Risk-Informed → Repeatable → Adaptive). The five-pillar model used in PQC Today's Crypto Management module (inventory, governance, lifecycle, observability, assurance) is this site's own teaching overlay, not a NIST taxonomy.
Acronym: NIST Cybersecurity White Paper 39
Category: standard

GL:cve.full:
A standardized identifier system for publicly known cybersecurity vulnerabilities, maintained by MITRE with CISA sponsorship, so a single CVE ID can be cross-referenced across advisories, scanners, and databases like the NVD.
Acronym: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures
Category: concept

GL:cyclonedx.full:
An OWASP standard for Software and Cryptography Bills of Materials (SBOM/CBOM). CycloneDX v1.6 introduced the Cryptography Asset type, enabling machine-readable inventory of all cryptographic algorithms, keys, certificates, and protocols in a system.
Category: standard

GL:data-asset-sensitivity.full:
A classification of how much harm would result if a data asset were exposed, altered, or made unavailable. Sensitivity tiers (Low, Medium, High, Critical) drive prioritisation of PQC migration effort and determine which assets face the greatest HNDL risk.
Category: concept

GL:data-encryption-key.full:
A symmetric key used to directly encrypt data. In envelope encryption architectures, the DEK is a short-lived, per-object AES key that encrypts actual data, while a Key Encryption Key (KEK) protects the DEK.
Acronym: DEK
Category: concept

GL:data-minimization.full:
The GDPR principle (Article 5(1)(c)) requiring personal data to be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purposes for which it is processed. Selective disclosure can support minimization technically, but it does not by itself establish necessity or enforce purpose limitation; that depends on the policy that decides which claims are requested and how they are used.
Category: concept

GL:data-retention-period.full:
The duration for which data must remain confidential or legally protected. Combined with the expected CRQC arrival year, the retention period determines the HNDL risk window: assets retained past the CRQC threshold are at immediate harvest risk.
Category: concept

GL:dda.full:
Dynamic Data Authentication. An EMV card authentication method where the card generates a unique RSA signature per transaction, preventing cloning attacks.
Acronym: DDA
Category: protocol

GL:deep-packet-inspection.full:
A network traffic analysis technique that examines packet payloads (not just headers) to classify, filter, or log traffic. Used by firewalls, IDS/IPS, and network monitoring tools to enforce security policies.
Acronym: DPI
Category: concept

GL:delegation-token.full:
A cryptographically signed credential that grants an AI agent limited authority to act on behalf of a user or another agent, with specified scope, duration, and capability constraints.
Category: concept

GL:demonstrating-proof-of-possession.full:
An OAuth 2.0 extension (RFC 9449) that binds tokens to a key and requires a signed proof when using a DPoP-bound token. Servers must validate the proof and token binding. This limits misuse of a stolen token without the key; it does not itself authenticate the client or prevent every replay attack.
Acronym: DPoP
Category: protocol

GL:der.full:
Distinguished Encoding Rules, a binary encoding format for ASN.1 data structures. The standard encoding for X.509 certificates, keys, and ECDSA signatures.
Acronym: DER
Category: concept

GL:der-distributed-energy-resource.full:
Distributed Energy Resource. Solar inverters, battery storage systems, and EV chargers connected to the distribution grid. Not to be confused with DER the ASN.1 encoding (Distinguished Encoding Rules).
Acronym: DER
Category: concept

GL:derivation-path.full:
A hierarchical path notation (e.g., m/44'/0'/0'/0/0) used in HD wallets to deterministically derive child keys from a master key following BIP32/BIP44 standards.
Category: concept

GL:device-attestation.full:
The process of cryptographically proving a device's identity and integrity to a remote verifier. Allows a server to verify that a device is what it claims to be and that its firmware/software has not been tampered with.
Category: concept

GL:device-binding.full:
Cryptographic proof that the entity presenting a credential controls the private key the credential was bound to at issuance.
Category: concept

GL:device-identity-key.full:
IEEE 802.1AR Initial Device Identity — a long-lived, factory-provisioned key used to prove device identity in network onboarding. The IEEE 802.1 amendment project P802.1AReg adds ML-DSA (the ML-DSA-44, ML-DSA-65 and ML-DSA-87 parameter sets) to 802.1AR; whether an existing device can hold an ML-DSA identity depends on what its hardware supports.
Acronym: IDevID
Category: concept

GL:dice.full:
Device Identifier Composition Engine — a hardware security architecture that uses a secret Unique Device Secret (UDS) and firmware measurement to derive a Compound Device Identifier (CDI), creating a hardware root of trust that is unique per device and firmware state.
Acronym: DICE
Category: concept

GL:dicom.full:
Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine. The standard protocol for transmitting, storing, and sharing medical images (X-ray, CT, MRI). DICOM supports TLS for transport security; PQC migration requires updating both the transport layer and any encrypted archives of imaging data.
Acronym: DICOM
Category: protocol

GL:diffie-hellman.full:
The original public-key key exchange protocol, allowing two parties to establish a shared secret over an insecure channel. Quantum-vulnerable.
Acronym: DH
Category: algorithm

GL:digital-signature.full:
A mathematical scheme that proves the authenticity and integrity of a digital message or document, analogous to a handwritten signature.
Category: concept

GL:digital-signatures.full:
Mathematical stamps that prove a message or file genuinely came from a specific person or server.
Category: concept

GL:dilithium.full:
The original name (CRYSTALS-Dilithium) for the lattice-based signature scheme standardized by NIST as ML-DSA in FIPS 204.
Category: algorithm

GL:disa.full:
US Department of Defense combat-support agency that runs IT infrastructure for the joint warfighter. Maintains the STIG library that locks down DoD system configurations, including cryptographic-suite controls.
Acronym: Defense Information Systems Agency
Category: organization

GL:dlms-cosem.full:
Device Language Message Specification / Companion Specification for Energy Metering. Used globally for smart meter communication with security suites based on AES and ECDSA/ECDH.
Acronym: DLMS/COSEM
Category: protocol

GL:dnp3-sa.full:
DNP3 Secure Authentication, the authentication mechanism for the DNP3 protocol (IEEE Std 1815), based on IEC 62351-5. Challenge-response authentication for SCADA using a message authentication code, with session keys protected by an Update Key that is pre-shared by default. IEEE 1815.1 is a different standard: the DNP3 to IEC 61850 mapping.
Acronym: DNP3-SA
Category: protocol

GL:dnssec.full:
DNS Security Extensions, a suite of protocols that add cryptographic authentication to DNS responses. Uses digital signatures to prevent DNS spoofing.
Acronym: DNSSEC
Category: protocol

GL:do-178c.full:
Software Considerations in Airborne Systems and Equipment Certification. The primary standard for certifying safety-critical avionics software, defining five Design Assurance Levels (DAL A through E).
Category: standard

GL:do-326a.full:
Airworthiness Security Process Specification. The FAA/EASA standard for addressing cybersecurity threats to airborne systems, requiring threat assessment and security controls for type certification.
Category: standard

GL:dod.full:
Department of Defense, the U.S. military department that mandates CNSA 2.0 compliance for National Security Systems and drives PQC migration timelines across defense contractors and suppliers.
Acronym: DoD
Category: organization

GL:domain-separated-hashing.full:
A technique that prepends a unique prefix byte to hash inputs depending on their type, preventing one type of hash from being confused with another. In Merkle trees, leaf hashes use prefix 0x00 and internal node hashes use prefix 0x01, as specified in RFC 9162.
Category: concept

GL:dora.full:
Digital Operational Resilience Act — EU Regulation 2022/2554, applying to financial entities and their ICT service providers from 17 January 2025. Requires an ICT risk management framework, resilience testing, and third-party risk oversight. Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774 requires an encryption and cryptographic-controls policy that provides for updating cryptographic technology as cryptanalysis develops; neither text sets a post-quantum migration date.
Acronym: DORA
Category: standard

GL:drbg.full:
Deterministic Random Bit Generator. An algorithm that produces a sequence of pseudorandom bits from a secret seed value. NIST SP 800-90A defines three approved mechanisms: CTR_DRBG, Hash_DRBG, and HMAC_DRBG.
Acronym: DRBG
Category: algorithm

GL:drm.full:
Digital Rights Management, technology protecting copyrighted content through encryption. Systems like Widevine, PlayReady, and FairPlay face quantum threats to their key hierarchies.
Acronym: DRM
Category: concept

GL:dsa.full:
Digital Signature Algorithm, a classical signature scheme based on discrete logarithms, specified in FIPS 186-4. FIPS 186-5 (February 2023) no longer approves DSA for generating digital signatures; DSA may only be used to verify signatures generated before that standard's implementation date. FIPS 186-4 was withdrawn on 3 February 2024.
Acronym: DSA
Category: algorithm

GL:dtls.full:
Datagram Transport Layer Security, the UDP equivalent of TLS. Used in IoT (CoAP), WebRTC, and VPN protocols. DTLS 1.3 adds PQC support.
Acronym: DTLS
Category: protocol

GL:dukpt.full:
Derived Unique Key Per Transaction, a key management scheme for payment terminals in which each terminal receives an initial key derived from a Base Derivation Key and uses it to derive a unique symmetric encryption key for each transaction.
Acronym: DUKPT
Category: concept

GL:dynamic-secrets.full:
Secrets generated on-demand with a short TTL and automatically revoked when the lease expires. Replaces long-lived static credentials with ephemeral ones that expire after the requesting workload is done.
Category: concept

GL:eal.full:
Common Criteria scoring scale from EAL1 (lowest) to EAL7 (highest) that grades the depth and rigor of a product's security evaluation. Higher EAL means more design analysis, more testing, and stronger evidence requirements — not necessarily a more secure product.
Acronym: Evaluation Assurance Level
Category: standard

GL:east-west-traffic.full:
Network traffic that flows laterally between servers, containers, or services within a data centre or cloud environment — as opposed to north-south traffic which flows between users and services across the network perimeter.
Category: concept

GL:ecc.full:
Elliptic Curve Cryptography — a public-key cryptosystem based on the algebraic structure of elliptic curves over finite fields. Offers smaller key sizes than RSA for equivalent classical security, but like RSA it is fully broken by Shor's algorithm on a CRQC.
Acronym: ECC
Category: algorithm

GL:ecdh.full:
Elliptic Curve Diffie-Hellman, a classical key agreement protocol. Quantum-vulnerable and being replaced by ML-KEM.
Acronym: ECDH
Category: algorithm

GL:ecdsa.full:
Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm, a classical signature scheme used in TLS, Bitcoin, and many other systems. Quantum-vulnerable.
Acronym: ECDSA
Category: algorithm

GL:ecies.full:
Elliptic Curve Integrated Encryption Scheme, used in 5G networks to conceal subscriber identity (SUCI). Combines ECDH key agreement with symmetric encryption.
Acronym: ECIES
Category: algorithm

GL:ed25519.full:
A high-performance digital signature algorithm using the Edwards curve Curve25519. Used in SSH, TLS, and Solana.
Category: algorithm

GL:ed448.full:
An EdDSA signature algorithm using the Edwards curve Curve448, providing 224-bit security. Quantum-vulnerable.
Category: algorithm

GL:eddsa.full:
Edwards-curve Digital Signature Algorithm, the family of signature schemes including Ed25519 and Ed448. Offers high performance and resistance to side-channel attacks.
Category: algorithm

GL:edge-pop.full:
A Point of Presence — a physical data center location at the network edge where CDN or cloud providers deploy servers to cache content and terminate TLS connections close to end users.
Acronym: PoP
Category: concept

GL:ehr.full:
Electronic Health Records, digital patient medical records that require long-term confidentiality. Prime targets for Harvest Now, Decrypt Later attacks.
Acronym: EHR
Category: concept

GL:eidas.full:
EU regulation (No 910/2014) governing electronic identification and trust services across member states. Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (eIDAS 2.0) establishes the European Digital Identity Framework: each Member State must provide at least one European Digital Identity Wallet within 24 months of the entry into force of the implementing acts. The amending text sets no post-quantum requirements.
Acronym: electronic IDentification, Authentication and trust Services
Category: standard

GL:eidas-2-0.full:
The EU regulation establishing a framework for electronic identification and trust services, including the European Digital Identity Wallet.
Category: standard

GL:eidas-trust-framework.full:
The cross-border mechanism ensuring mutual recognition of digital identities, wallets and qualified attestations across all 27 EU member states.
Category: concept

GL:electronic-control-unit.full:
An embedded computer in a vehicle that controls one or more electrical systems (engine, brakes, infotainment). Automotive ECUs communicate via CAN bus and face PQC migration challenges for V2X and firmware signing.
Acronym: ECU
Category: concept

GL:elliptic-curve-cryptography.full:
A classical public-key algorithm using the mathematics of elliptic curves. More efficient than RSA but equally vulnerable to quantum attacks.
Acronym: ECC
Category: algorithm

GL:emv.full:
Europay/Mastercard/Visa, the global standard for chip-based payment card authentication. Uses RSA and ECC signatures that are quantum-vulnerable.
Acronym: EMV
Category: protocol

GL:encapsulation-decapsulation.full:
The two operations of a Key Encapsulation Mechanism. Encapsulation creates a shared secret using a public key; decapsulation recovers it using the private key.
Category: concept

GL:enclave.full:
An isolated execution environment inside a trusted execution environment (TEE) in which code and data are protected from the other software on the host. What lies outside the protection boundary, such as the operating system or hypervisor, and how memory is protected differ between platforms, so check the platform's documented threat model.
Category: concept

GL:encrypted-payload.full:
The secure container wrapping IKEv2 payloads like Identifiers (IDi/IDr), Certificates (CERT), and Authentication (AUTH) data.
Acronym: SK
Category: protocol

GL:encryption.full:
The process of converting readable data (plaintext) into an unreadable format (ciphertext) using an algorithm and a key, so only authorized parties can read it.
Category: concept

GL:endorsement-key.full:
A TPM 2.0 primary key in the Endorsement hierarchy (handle TPM_RH_ENDORSEMENT = 0x4000000B), derived from the Endorsement Primary Seed and certified by the manufacturer to establish trust in the TPM. TPM 2.0 library version 185 (March 2026) adds ML-KEM keys (TPM_ALG_MLKEM = 0x00A0), and the TCG EK Credential Profile 2.7 defines ML-KEM EK templates alongside the RSA and ECC ones, so a TPM can have EKs of several algorithms. A storage-type EK is used for credential activation.
Acronym: EK
Category: concept

GL:enisa.full:
European Union Agency for Cybersecurity, publishing PQC guidelines and coordinating quantum-safe transitions across EU member states.
Acronym: ENISA
Category: organization

GL:entanglement.full:
A quantum phenomenon in which two or more qubits share a joint state, so their measurement results are correlated more strongly than any pre-agreed classical rule could explain, even when the qubits are far apart.
Category: concept

GL:entropy.full:
A measure of unpredictability or randomness in data. In cryptography, high entropy means data is difficult to predict, which is essential for secure key generation and nonce creation.
Category: concept

GL:entropy-source-validation.full:
The CMVP process for validating an entropy source — the combination of a noise source, health tests and an optional conditioning component that produces random bitstrings for a random bit generator — against NIST SP 800-90B. An accredited laboratory tests the entropy source and submits it through NIST's Entropy Source Validation Test System (ESVTS), and a validated entropy source may be referenced by certificate number in multiple modules without being recertified.
Acronym: ESV
Category: concept

GL:envelope-encryption.full:
A two-level encryption scheme: a data encryption key (DEK) encrypts the data, and a key encryption key (KEK) encrypts the DEK. The encrypted DEK is stored alongside the ciphertext. Only the KEK needs to be protected in a KMS.
Category: concept

GL:envelopeddata.full:
A CMS structure for encrypted content using key transport (RSA) or key agreement (ECDH). Being superseded by AuthEnvelopedData with KEM-based encryption for PQC.
Category: protocol

GL:ephi.full:
Electronic Protected Health Information — individually identifiable health information in electronic form, regulated by HIPAA. Any encryption of ePHI using RSA or ECC is vulnerable to HNDL attacks, making ePHI datasets a high-priority PQC migration target.
Acronym: ePHI
Category: concept

GL:est.full:
IETF certificate enrollment protocol (RFC 7030) used by devices to request, renew, and re-key X.509 certificates over TLS. Common in IoT, enterprise PKI, and 802.1X NAC enrolment.
Acronym: Enrollment over Secure Transport
Category: protocol

GL:etsi.full:
European Telecommunications Standards Institute, producing PQC migration guides and standards for European industry.
Acronym: ETSI
Category: organization

GL:eucc.full:
EU Cybersecurity Certification Scheme — the European Union's harmonized product security certification scheme based on Common Criteria, adopted by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/482 under the EU Cybersecurity Act (2019).
Acronym: EUCC
Category: standard

GL:eudi-wallet.full:
European Union Digital Identity Wallet, a mobile wallet for storing and presenting digital credentials under the eIDAS 2.0 framework.
Category: concept

GL:euroqci.full:
The European Quantum Communication Infrastructure initiative, a pan-EU program to deploy a quantum communication network across all 27 member states combining terrestrial fiber and satellite links.
Acronym: EuroQCI
Category: organization

GL:executive-order.full:
A directive issued by the U.S. President to federal agencies, carrying the force of law without requiring Congressional approval. Executive Order 14412, "Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks" (June 22, 2026), is the order currently driving federal PQC migration deadlines.
Acronym: EO
Category: concept

GL:extended-key-usage.full:
An X.509 certificate extension that restricts the purposes for which a certificate can be used — for example, Code Signing (OID 1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.3), Server Authentication, or Client Authentication.
Acronym: EKU
Category: concept

GL:faest.full:
An MPC-in-the-Head signature candidate in the NIST signature on-ramp. Builds a signature out of a simulated multi-party computation over the AES block cipher.
Category: algorithm

GL:fair-model.full:
Factor Analysis of Information Risk — a quantitative risk methodology that models cybersecurity risk in financial terms. Decomposes risk into Loss Event Frequency (how often a loss occurs, itself Threat Event Frequency combined with Vulnerability, the probability that a threat event becomes a loss) and Loss Magnitude, to produce an annualized loss estimate.
Acronym: FAIR
Category: concept

GL:falcon.full:
The NTRU-lattice-based signature scheme selected by NIST as the basis for the planned FN-DSA standard. FIPS 206 remains in development with no published Initial Public Draft or final standard.
Category: algorithm

GL:fault-injection.full:
An active implementation attack that deliberately induces a physical fault — voltage or clock glitching, laser pulses, electromagnetic pulses — during a cryptographic operation to force an incorrect computation and leak secret material.
Category: concept

GL:federated-learning.full:
A machine learning approach where models are trained across multiple decentralized devices or servers holding local data samples, without exchanging raw data — only encrypted model updates are shared.
Category: concept

GL:federation.full:
An identity trust relationship between two or more organizations that allows users from one organization to authenticate with another's services using their home organization's credentials. Enables SSO across organizational boundaries.
Category: concept

GL:fedramp.full:
Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program — a U.S. government-wide program that provides a standardized approach to security assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring for cloud products and services used by federal agencies.
Acronym: FedRAMP
Category: standard

GL:fido2-webauthn.full:
Web authentication standards enabling passwordless login using public-key cryptography. Currently relies on quantum-vulnerable ECDSA/EdDSA.
Category: protocol

GL:filing-date.full:
The date a complete patent application was formally submitted to the patent office. It anchors the start of prosecution and (for the earliest non-provisional filing in a family) the patent term calculation.
Category: concept

GL:fips-140-2.full:
The predecessor to FIPS 140-3 for validating cryptographic modules. NIST's CMVP stopped accepting new FIPS 140-2 submissions in 2021; many previously validated modules remain listed during a multi-year transition to FIPS 140-3.
Category: standard

GL:fips-140-3.full:
The U.S. government standard for validating cryptographic modules. Hardware and software must pass FIPS 140-3 testing to be used in federal systems.
Category: standard

GL:fips-140-3-mode.full:
An operating-system setting that restricts cryptographic operations to the algorithms and settings permitted under FIPS 140. FIPS 140-3 validates cryptographic modules, not settings, so a system uses validated cryptography only if the modules it relies on hold a current validation certificate. U.S. federal agencies that require cryptographic protection must use validated modules.
Category: concept

GL:fips-186-5.full:
The NIST Digital Signature Standard defining RSA, ECDSA, and EdDSA. Being deprecated in favor of PQC signature algorithms per NIST IR 8547.
Category: standard

GL:fips-199.full:
Federal Information Processing Standard 199 — NIST's standard for categorising federal information and information systems. Defines three impact levels (Low, Moderate, High) for confidentiality, integrity, and availability that drive control selection in the NIST RMF.
Category: standard

GL:fips-203.full:
The NIST standard defining ML-KEM (Module-Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism), published August 2024.
Category: standard

GL:fips-204.full:
The NIST standard defining ML-DSA (Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm), published August 2024.
Category: standard

GL:fips-205.full:
The NIST standard defining SLH-DSA (Stateless Hash-Based Digital Signature Algorithm), published August 2024.
Category: standard

GL:fips-206.full:
The planned NIST standard for FN-DSA (FFT over NTRU-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm, based on Falcon). FIPS 206 is still in development; NIST has not published an Initial Public Draft or final standard.
Category: standard

GL:firmware-signing.full:
The process of cryptographically signing firmware images before distribution and verifying the signature before execution. Ensures that firmware has not been tampered with since it was signed by the vendor.
Category: concept

GL:fleet-migration.full:
The coordinated process of upgrading cryptographic configurations across an entire fleet of servers, endpoints, IoT devices, and network appliances to support post-quantum algorithms, typically executed in phased rollouts with rollback capability.
Category: concept

GL:fn-dsa.full:
FFT over NTRU-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm, based on Falcon, and planned for FIPS 206. FIPS 206 remains in development; no Initial Public Draft or final standard has been published.
Category: algorithm

GL:formal-verification.full:
Mathematical proof techniques used to verify that cryptographic algorithm implementations correctly conform to their specifications, providing stronger assurance than testing alone. Critical for PQC algorithms where implementation subtleties can introduce vulnerabilities.
Category: concept

GL:fors.full:
The few-time signature component of SLH-DSA (FIPS 205). It signs part of the message digest using k hash trees of height a. The hypertree authenticates the resulting FORS public key.
Acronym: Forest of Random Subsets
Category: algorithm

GL:forward-secrecy.full:
A property of key exchange protocols where compromise of long-term keys does not compromise past session keys. Each session uses ephemeral keys that are discarded.
Category: concept

GL:frodokem.full:
