A conservative lattice-based KEM algorithm based on the "plain" Learning With Errors problem, offering strong security guarantees at the cost of larger key sizes.
Category: algorithm

GL:fulcio.full:
The Certificate Authority component of Sigstore. Fulcio issues short-lived X.509 certificates, valid for 10 minutes, that bind an OIDC identity to an ephemeral signing key.
Category: concept

GL:fully-homomorphic-encryption.full:
An encryption scheme that allows computations to be performed on ciphertext, producing encrypted results that match operations on the plaintext.
Acronym: FHE
Category: concept

GL:gdpr.full:
General Data Protection Regulation — EU Regulation 2016/679 requiring controllers and processors to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect personal data. Article 32 lists pseudonymisation and encryption among the measures to consider, judged against the state of the art, cost and risk. The regulation names no algorithms and sets no post-quantum migration date.
Acronym: GDPR
Category: standard

GL:gemss.full:
A multivariate-quadratic signature scheme and NIST PQC Round 3 alternate candidate, notable for very large public keys; not selected for standardization.
Acronym: Great Multivariate Short Signature
Category: algorithm

GL:gina.full:
Genetic Information Nondiscrimination Act (2008). US federal law prohibiting discrimination based on genetic information in health insurance and employment. Genetic data decrypted via HNDL attacks could enable discrimination that GINA was designed to prevent.
Acronym: GINA
Category: standard

GL:globalplatform.full:
An industry association that standardizes secure-element and trusted-execution-environment specifications used in SIM cards, secure elements, and IoT hardware roots of trust, now extending its specifications to PQC-capable secure elements.
Category: organization

GL:gnutls-priority-string.full:
A configuration syntax used in GnuTLS to specify which TLS protocol versions, cipher suites, and key exchange algorithms are acceptable. Used in Linux systems as the TLS policy configuration for applications using the GnuTLS library.
Category: concept

GL:goose.full:
Generic Object Oriented Substation Event. A high-speed multicast protocol in the IEC 61850 series, used for time-critical messages such as protection relay tripping.
Acronym: GOOSE
Category: protocol

GL:governance-risk-and-compliance.full:
The organisational function that measures, reports on, and governs risk — as distinct from a SOC, which detects and responds to it. GRC produces the instruments a board uses for oversight, a CISO uses to manage a program, and internal audit uses to verify it.
Acronym: GRC
Category: concept

GL:grover-s-algorithm.full:
A quantum algorithm offering a quadratic speedup for unstructured search in an idealized query model. Practical cryptanalytic cost depends on implementation resources; hash collision search and preimage search are different goals.
Category: algorithm

GL:gsma.full:
Global System for Mobile Communications Association, leading the Post-Quantum Telco Network Taskforce for PQC integration in mobile networks.
Acronym: GSMA
Category: organization

GL:harvest-now-decrypt-later.full:
An attack strategy where adversaries collect encrypted data today with the intention of decrypting it once quantum computers become available.
Acronym: HNDL
Category: concept

GL:harvest-now-forge-later.full:
An attack strategy against digital signatures: once quantum computers can break the signing algorithm, an adversary can forge new signed artifacts without capturing anything first. Archived signatures are affected too: whether they can still be trusted depends on whether evidence of when they were made has been preserved. Also called Trust Now, Forge Later (TNFL); the two terms are interchangeable and used equally across the platform.
Acronym: HNFL
Category: concept

GL:hash-based.full:
Digital signatures built from hash functions. They help check who signed data and whether it changed; they do not hide the data.
Category: concept

GL:hash-based-signatures.full:
Digital signature schemes whose security relies only on the properties of hash functions. Very conservative security but can be stateful.
Category: concept

GL:hawk.full:
A lattice-based signature scheme that NIST advanced to the third round of its additional-signature process in May 2026; its team withdrew it on 29 July 2026, so it is no longer a candidate. It was designed as an integer-only alternative to FN-DSA (Falcon) and avoids the floating-point operations that complicate Falcon implementations.
Category: algorithm

GL:hd-wallet.full:
Hierarchical Deterministic Wallet, a cryptocurrency wallet that generates all key pairs from a single seed phrase using BIP32/39/44 standards.
Acronym: HD
Category: concept

GL:header.full:
The fixed header at the start of every IKEv2 message (HDR). It is not encrypted: it carries the SPIs, version numbers, exchange type, message ID and flags in the clear. When a message includes an Encrypted payload, the header is covered by that message's integrity protection.
Acronym: HDR
Category: protocol

GL:hedged-signing.full:
A signing mode for ML-DSA (FIPS 204) that incorporates additional randomness alongside the deterministic component, providing protection against fault injection and side-channel attacks that attempt to recover the private key by manipulating the signing process.
Category: concept

GL:hipaa.full:
Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, a U.S. law whose Security Rule requires covered entities and business associates to protect electronic protected health information. Encryption is an addressable specification: it must be assessed and implemented where reasonable and appropriate, or the reason documented and an equivalent measure used. Patient data faces HNDL risk.
Acronym: HIPAA
Category: standard

GL:hkdf.full:
HMAC-based Key Derivation Function, used to derive cryptographic keys from a shared secret. Essential in TLS 1.3.
Acronym: HKDF
Category: algorithm

GL:hmac.full:
Hash-based Message Authentication Code, a keyed construction that combines a secret key with a hash function (e.g. SHA-256) to provide message integrity and authenticity.
Acronym: HMAC
Category: algorithm

GL:hmac-sha-256.full: Hash-based MAC using SHA-256; provides integrity + authenticity of a message.

GL:hmac-sha3-256.full: HMAC using SHA3-256. This site's 5G SUCI workshop uses it as the MAC of its experimental ML-KEM "Profile C", which is not a 3GPP profile (3GPP Profiles A and B use HMAC-SHA-256).

GL:hndl-risk-window.full:
The period during which data harvested today could realistically be decrypted by a future CRQC. Calculated as the gap between the estimated CRQC arrival year and the data's required confidentiality end date.
Category: concept

GL:homomorphic-encryption.full:
An encryption scheme that allows computations to be performed directly on encrypted data without decrypting it first, producing encrypted results that match what would be obtained from the plaintext.
Acronym: HE
Category: concept

GL:hqc.full:
Hamming Quasi-Cyclic, a code-based KEM selected by NIST as an additional standard. Uses error-correcting codes for security.
Category: algorithm

GL:hsm.full:
Hardware Security Module, a dedicated physical device for managing and protecting cryptographic keys. Must be updated for PQC support.
Acronym: HSM
Category: concept

GL:hss.full:
RFC 8554 stateful hash-based signature scheme that composes multiple LMS trees into a single signing capability with extended lifetime. PQC-relevant for firmware / software signing where the key state can be tracked.
Acronym: Hierarchical Signature System
Category: concept

GL:human-machine-interface.full:
A user interface panel or software application that allows operators to monitor and control industrial processes. HMIs sit at Purdue Level 2, typically using RSA-2048 or TLS 1.2.
Acronym: HMI
Category: concept

GL:hybrid-certificate.full:
An X.509 certificate that carries both classical and post-quantum public keys during the transition period. Legacy interoperability depends on the design: a composite certificate is understood only by upgraded systems, while other designs let a verifier that has not migrated rely on the classical part.
Category: concept

GL:hybrid-cryptography.full:
Using classical and post-quantum algorithms together during the transition period. A well-designed hybrid stays secure as long as at least one algorithm remains secure; the guarantee depends on how the algorithms are combined and implemented.
Category: concept

GL:hybrid-key-exchange.full:
Combining a classical key exchange (e.g., X25519) with a PQC KEM (e.g., ML-KEM-768) in a single handshake, so the derived secret stays secure as long as at least one of the two components remains unbroken and the combination is well designed.
Category: concept

GL:hybrid-migration.full:
A PQC transition strategy in which a classical algorithm and a post-quantum algorithm are used together in the same protocol, so that a well-designed combination stays secure if one of them is broken. Agency guidance differs: BSI and ANSSI recommend hybrid schemes for the transition, NIST leaves the decision to each application, and the UK NCSC advises treating hybrid as an interim measure if it is chosen.
Category: concept

GL:hybrid-mode.full:
An operational mode where classical and post-quantum cryptographic algorithms run together, intended to keep security if one of them is broken when the combination is well designed.
Category: concept

GL:hybrid-public-key-encryption.full:
A standardized framework (RFC 9180) for hybrid public-key encryption that combines a KEM, a key derivation function, and an AEAD cipher into a composable primitive.
Acronym: HPKE
Category: protocol

GL:hyok.full:
Hold Your Own Key — a cloud encryption model where the customer holds a key that never leaves their on-premises HSM. The cloud service requests encryption operations from the customer HSM rather than using cloud-side keys.
Acronym: HYOK
Category: concept

GL:hypertree.full:
The SLH-DSA hypertree has d layers of XMSS trees, each of height h/d. The lowest layer signs FORS public keys; higher layers sign the roots of XMSS trees below them. The SLH-DSA public key contains both the public seed PK.seed and the top root PK.root.
Category: concept

GL:iccp-tase-2.full:
Inter-Control Center Communications Protocol (IEC 60870-6 TASE.2). Used for real-time data exchange between utility control centers; the IEC 62351 series defines TLS-based protection for it.
Acronym: ICCP
Category: protocol

GL:identity-provider.full:
A system that creates, maintains, and manages digital identities and their authentication. The IdP authenticates users and issues tokens (SAML assertions, JWT, OIDC ID tokens) that allow access to service providers.
Acronym: IdP
Category: concept

GL:ids-ips.full:
Intrusion Detection System / Intrusion Prevention System — network security tools that monitor traffic for known attack patterns (signature-based) or anomalous behaviour (anomaly-based). IPS operates inline and can block traffic; IDS is passive.
Acronym: IDS/IPS
Category: concept

GL:iec.full:
International Electrotechnical Commission, the international standards body for electrical and electronic technologies.
Acronym: IEC
Category: organization

GL:iec-61850.full:
International standard series for communication networks and systems in power utility automation, including substations. Its mappings cover MMS, GOOSE and Sampled Values for protection and control.
Category: standard

GL:iec-62351.full:
Power systems management and associated information exchange — security standard. Covers TLS profiles, GOOSE authentication, and key management for power systems.
Category: standard

GL:iec-62443.full:
International standard series for industrial automation and control systems (IACS) cybersecurity. Critical for IoT and energy sector PQC migration.
Category: standard

GL:ied.full:
Intelligent Electronic Device. Microprocessor-based controllers in substations (protection relays, bay controllers) with 20-25 year lifecycles.
Acronym: IED
Category: concept

GL:ieee.full:
Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers, a professional association that publishes technical standards — including IEEE 1609.2 (vehicular communications) and IEEE 2030.5 (smart grid), both already in this glossary — now being updated for PQC.
Acronym: IEEE
Category: organization

GL:ieee-1609-2.full:
The security standard for Wireless Access in Vehicular Environments (WAVE), defining V2X message signing, certificate formats, and the Security Credential Management System (SCMS) for pseudonym certificate issuance.
Category: standard

GL:ieee-2030-5.full:
Smart Energy Profile 2.0 standard for distributed energy resource communication using certificate-based device authentication.
Category: standard

GL:ietf.full:
Internet Engineering Task Force, developing PQC integration into internet protocols like TLS, SSH, and IKEv2.
Acronym: IETF
Category: organization

GL:ietf-plants-working-group.full:
The IETF working group responsible for standardizing Merkle Tree Certificates and related post-quantum PKI infrastructure. Adopted draft-ietf-plants-merkle-tree-certs in January 2026.
Acronym: PLANTS
Category: organization

GL:ike-auth.full:
The completion phase of the IKEv2 handshake. It authenticates the previous messages and establishes the first IPsec Security Association (CHILD_SA).
Category: protocol

GL:ike-intermediate.full:
An optional phase introduced in IKEv2 to transmit large amounts of data, such as post-quantum key shares, before authentication completes.
Category: protocol

GL:ike-sa-init.full:
The initial phase of the IKEv2 protocol. It negotiates cryptographic algorithms, exchanges nonces, and performs a Diffie-Hellman exchange.
Category: protocol

GL:ikev2.full:
Internet Key Exchange version 2, the protocol used to establish security associations in IPsec VPNs. PQC migration adds ML-KEM key exchange.
Acronym: IKEv2
Category: protocol

GL:in-toto.full:
An open-source framework for securing the integrity of software supply chains by defining and cryptographically verifying each step of the build and release process. Each step produces a signed attestation (a "link") forming a verifiable chain.
Category: standard

GL:inclusion-proof.full:
A compact chain of sibling hashes from a leaf to the root of a Merkle tree, proving that a specific item (such as a certificate) is part of the committed batch. Verification requires only hash recomputation, not signature verification.
Category: concept

GL:independent-claim.full:
A patent claim that stands alone and defines the invention completely without referring to any other claim. Every patent has at least one. Independent claims set the broadest scope of protection; dependent claims narrow an independent claim by adding further limitations and must be read together with it.
Category: concept

GL:information-theoretic-security.full:
A security guarantee that holds regardless of the adversary's computational power, including quantum computers, because it does not rest on a hardness assumption. QKD protocols are proven to offer this kind of security in a theoretical model, under conditions such as an authenticated classical channel.
Category: concept

GL:international-traffic-in-arms-regulat.full:
US export control regulations (22 CFR 120-130) governing the export and transfer of defense articles and services, including military cryptographic systems listed on the US Munitions List.
Acronym: ITAR
Category: standard

GL:interoperability.full:
The ability of different cryptographic implementations, libraries, and systems to work together correctly. Critical during PQC migration when classical and quantum-safe systems must coexist.
Category: concept

GL:interoperability-matrix.full:
A compatibility mapping showing which combinations of client and server PQC algorithm configurations successfully negotiate a shared secret. Used during the lab testing phase of PQC migration to identify which vendor combinations are compatible, require fallback, or are incompatible.
Category: concept

GL:iomt.full:
Internet of Medical Things. Network-connected medical devices including infusion pumps, cardiac monitors, and surgical robots. IoMT devices combine the constrained-resource challenges of IoT with the safety-critical requirements of medical devices, creating unique PQC migration challenges.
Acronym: IoMT
Category: concept

GL:ipsec.full:
Internet Protocol Security, a protocol suite for encrypting and authenticating IP traffic. Used in VPNs and site-to-site connections.
Acronym: IPsec
Category: protocol

GL:iso.full:
International Organization for Standardization, a Geneva-based body that develops and publishes international standards.
Acronym: ISO
Category: organization

GL:iso-15118.full:
An international standard for vehicle-to-grid communication enabling Plug & Charge: automatic mutual authentication between electric vehicles and charging stations using X.509 certificates over TLS.
Category: standard

GL:iso-27005.full:
ISO/IEC 27005 — the international standard for information security risk management. Provides a structured methodology for identifying assets, assessing threats and vulnerabilities, evaluating risk, and selecting risk treatment options.
Category: standard

GL:iso-iec-18013-5.full:
International standard for mobile driving licences (mDL), defining the data model, security mechanisms, and device engagement protocols for digital identity documents.
Category: standard

GL:iso-iec-27001.full:
International standard specifying requirements for an Information Security Management System (ISMS). Annex A.10 covers cryptography. Does not mandate PQC directly but the control framework drives PQC adoption.
Acronym: Information Security Management Systems
Category: standard

GL:iso-iec-jtc-1.full:
Joint Technical Committee 1 of ISO and IEC, the international standards body for information technology including cryptographic standards (SC 27).
Category: organization

GL:isogeny-based-cryptography.full:
PQC algorithms built on the hardness of finding isogenies (structure-preserving maps) between supersingular elliptic curves. Offers the smallest combined public key + signature sizes of any PQC family. SQIsign is the leading on-ramp candidate.
Category: concept

GL:issue-date.full:
The date a patent is formally granted and becomes enforceable — sometimes called the grant date. It marks the end of examination, when the patentee gains the legal right to exclude others from the claimed invention.
Category: concept

GL:itsm-cccs.full:
CCCS Canada's technical-guidance document series (ITSM.40.xxx, ITSAP.xx.xxx). The PQC-relevant entry today is ITSAP.00.017 — Preparing your organization for the quantum threat to cryptography.
Acronym: Information Technology Security Management series
Category: organization

GL:itu-t.full:
International Telecommunication Union — Telecommunication Standardization Sector. Study Group 17 (SG17) is developing PQC standards for telecommunications infrastructure.
Acronym: ITU-T
Category: organization

GL:jca-jce.full:
Java Cryptography Architecture / Extension — the standard Java framework for cryptographic operations. JCA provides the provider model and key management; JCE extends it with cipher and key agreement operations.
Acronym: JCA/JCE
Category: concept

GL:jcprov.full:
A Java wrapper for the PKCS#11 API from Thales (Luna), in jcprov.jar under the package com.safenetinc.jcprov. It is separate from the Luna JSP, which is the JCA/JCE provider.
Category: concept

GL:jose.full:
JSON Object Signing and Encryption, the IETF framework encompassing JWS, JWE, JWK, and JWA specifications. JOSE defines how to sign, encrypt, and represent cryptographic keys in JSON format.
Category: protocol

GL:json-web-encryption.full:
A standard (RFC 7516) for authenticated encryption of arbitrary plaintext bytes. Its key-management modes include encrypting or wrapping a content-encryption key (CEK), deriving it by key agreement, or using a shared symmetric CEK directly. Not every mode uses a separate wrapping key.
Acronym: JWE
Category: protocol

GL:json-web-key-set.full:
A JSON document (RFC 7517) containing an array of JSON Web Keys. Public JWKS endpoints commonly publish verification keys, but the format can also represent private or symmetric key material, which must not be disclosed publicly.
Acronym: JWKS
Category: protocol

GL:json-web-signature.full:
A standard (RFC 7515) for protecting arbitrary payload bytes with a digital signature or MAC. The protected JOSE header and payload are authenticated; JSON-serialization unprotected headers are not. A verifier must check the result using an accepted algorithm and trusted key.
Acronym: JWS
Category: protocol

GL:jwt.full:
JSON Web Token, a compact token format for securely transmitting claims between parties. Widely used in API authentication and OAuth 2.0.
Acronym: JWT
Category: protocol

GL:kdf.full:
Cryptographic function that derives one or more secret keys from a shared secret, password, or master key. PQC handshakes use HKDF (RFC 5869) to expand the KEM-output shared secret into traffic keys and resumption keys.
Acronym: Key Derivation Function
Category: concept

GL:keccak-256.full:
The hash function used by Ethereum, based on the SHA-3 algorithm family. Produces 256-bit digests.
Category: algorithm

GL:kem.full:
Cryptographic primitive that produces a ciphertext encapsulating a fresh shared secret under the recipient's public key. ML-KEM (FIPS 203) is the NIST-standardised PQC KEM; classical examples include RSA-KEM and DHKEM.
Acronym: Key Encapsulation Mechanism
Category: concept

GL:kemrecipientinfo.full:
A CMS recipient information structure defined in RFC 9629. A KEM establishes a pairwise shared secret; a KDF derives a key-encryption key (KEK), which wraps the content-encryption key (CEK) or content-authenticated-encryption key.
Category: protocol

GL:kerberos.full:
A network authentication protocol that uses symmetric key cryptography and a trusted third party (Key Distribution Center) to authenticate service requests. The dominant authentication protocol in Microsoft Active Directory environments.
Category: concept

GL:key-binding.full:
Cryptographic proof that a credential is bound to a specific holder's key, preventing unauthorized transfer or replay of digital credentials.
Category: concept

GL:key-encapsulation-mechanism.full:
A method to securely establish a shared secret key between two parties. The PQC replacement for traditional key exchange.
Acronym: KEM
Category: protocol

GL:key-exchange.full:
The process by which two parties establish a shared secret key over an insecure channel. In PQC, replaced by Key Encapsulation Mechanisms.
Category: concept

GL:key-exchange-key.full:
A UEFI Secure Boot key that is trusted to update the Signature Database (db) and Revocation Database (dbx). Updates to the KEK list itself must be signed by the Platform Key (PK), and the KEK lets OS vendors add their own signing certificates to the Secure Boot databases.
Acronym: KEK
Category: concept

GL:key-injection-facility.full:
A physically secured facility where cryptographic keys are loaded into payment terminals under dual-control, split-knowledge procedures.
Acronym: KIF
Category: concept

GL:key-lifecycle.full:
The complete management process for cryptographic keys from creation to destruction. NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 divides it into four phases (pre-operational, operational, post-operational and destroyed); this site teaches it as seven practical stages: generation, storage, activation, rotation, deactivation, compromise response, and destruction.
Category: concept

GL:key-pair.full:
A mathematically linked public key and private key used together for encryption/decryption or signing/verification.
Category: concept

GL:key-performance-indicator.full:
A quantifiable metric used to measure progress toward organizational objectives. In PQC programs, KPIs track inventory completion, migration progress, vendor readiness, compliance gaps, and budget utilization.
Acronym: KPI
Category: concept

GL:key-rotation.full:
The practice of periodically replacing cryptographic keys with new ones, limiting the exposure window if a key is compromised.
Category: concept

GL:key-rotation-database.full:
The process of replacing an active database encryption key with a new one, re-encrypting data (or key metadata) under the new key, and retiring the old key. Critical for limiting cryptographic exposure over time.
Category: concept

GL:key-size-impact.full:
The significant increase in cryptographic key and signature sizes when migrating from classical to post-quantum algorithms. ML-KEM public keys are 800–1568 bytes (vs. 32–91 for ECC), and ML-DSA signatures are 2420–4627 bytes (vs. 64–72 for ECDSA), affecting APIs, protocols, and storage.
Category: concept

GL:keyless-signing.full:
A code signing approach where the developer does not keep a long-term signing key. A short-lived key pair is generated per signing event, and a CA (for example Sigstore Fulcio) issues a short-lived certificate binding that key to an OIDC identity; the signing is recorded in a transparency log so it can be verified after the certificate expires. Trust moves to the identity provider, the CA and the log; keys are still used.
Category: concept

GL:kisa.full:
South Korea's national agency for cybersecurity and internet governance. Operates the K-CMVP cryptographic-module validation programme and co-administers the KpqC competition with academic partners.
Acronym: Korea Internet & Security Agency
Category: organization

GL:kmip.full:
Key Management Interoperability Protocol, an OASIS standard for communication between key management systems and cryptographic clients.
Acronym: KMIP
Category: protocol

GL:kms.full:
Key Management System, software for generating, storing, rotating, and auditing cryptographic keys. Must be upgraded to support PQC key sizes and algorithms.
Acronym: KMS
Category: concept

GL:known-answer-test.full:
A kind of cryptographic algorithm self-test in which a module operates an algorithm on a set of known input vectors and compares the result to the known expected output; if the calculated output does not equal the known answer, the self-test fails. The FIPS 140-3 Implementation Guidance calls it the most common way to meet an algorithm self-test requirement, alongside comparison tests and fault-detection tests.
Acronym: KAT
Category: concept

GL:kpqc.full:
Korean Post-Quantum Cryptography project, South Korea's national initiative to develop and standardize its own PQC algorithms including HAETAE, AIMer, SMAUG-T, and NTRU+.
Acronym: KpqC
Category: organization

GL:ksp.full:
Key Storage Provider — a Windows CNG component that manages private key isolation and storage. KSPs abstract over software (MS_KEY_STORAGE_PROVIDER), TPM (MS_PLATFORM_KEY_STORAGE_PROVIDER), and HSM-backed storage.
Acronym: KSP
Category: concept

GL:kyber.full:
The original name (CRYSTALS-Kyber) for the lattice-based KEM standardized by NIST as ML-KEM in FIPS 203. Often still referenced in older documents and libraries.
Category: algorithm

GL:kyverno.full:
A Kubernetes-native policy engine that validates, mutates, and generates resources using YAML-based ClusterPolicies. Used to enforce PQC requirements: blocking unsigned or ECDSA-only container images, requiring ML-DSA image signatures, and enforcing X-Wing cipher suites on Ingress resources.
Category: concept

GL:lamps.full:
The IETF working group producing PQC and composite-signature specifications for X.509 certificates, CMS, and S/MIME — including the composite ML-DSA drafts this hub's own email-signing workshop implements.
Acronym: Limited Additional Mechanisms for PKIX and SMIME
Category: protocol

GL:lattice-based.full:
A type of math puzzle based on plotting points in a massive grid, used to build safe encryption.
Category: concept

GL:lattice-based-cryptography.full:
A family of PQC algorithms based on the hardness of problems involving mathematical lattices. The basis for ML-KEM and ML-DSA.
Category: concept

GL:ldap.full:
The protocol used to query and update directory services such as Microsoft Active Directory — the store of user accounts, groups, and credentials that authentication systems rely on.
Acronym: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol
Category: concept

GL:learning-with-errors.full:
A mathematical problem believed to be hard for quantum computers, forming the security foundation of ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and FrodoKEM.
Acronym: LWE
Category: concept

GL:lease-renewal.full:
The time-bounded validity period of a secret or token in a secrets manager. Every dynamically generated secret has a lease — it expires unless explicitly renewed before the TTL elapses.
Category: concept

GL:lgpd.full:
Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados — Brazil's data protection law (Law 13.709/2018), modelled on GDPR. Article 46 requires processing agents to adopt technical and administrative security measures to protect personal data from unauthorised access and from accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration or improper processing. The national authority (ANPD) may set minimum technical standards; the law text does not mention encryption.
Acronym: LGPD
Category: standard

GL:liboqs.full:
Open Quantum Safe C library — the reference implementation hub for post-quantum cryptographic algorithms. Maintained by the Open Quantum Safe project and serves as the foundation for oqsprovider, oqs-go, liboqs-python, and other language bindings.
Category: concept

GL:line-replaceable-unit.full:
A modular avionics component designed to be quickly swapped on an aircraft during maintenance without extensive disassembly, enabling field-level repairs.
Acronym: LRU
Category: concept

GL:lm-ots.full:
The one-time signature primitive underlying LMS: each LM-OTS key pair is valid for exactly one signature, and many are combined via a Merkle tree to build a reusable LMS key.
Acronym: Leighton-Micali One-Time Signature
Category: algorithm

GL:lms.full:
Leighton-Micali Signature — a stateful hash-based signature scheme standardised in NIST SP 800-208 and RFC 8554. Built from LM-OTS one-time signatures, a Winternitz-style scheme, combined in a Merkle tree. Approved by CNSA 2.0 for firmware and software signing.
Acronym: LMS
Category: algorithm

GL:lms-hss.full:
Leighton-Micali Signature / Hierarchical Signature System. A stateful hash-based signature scheme for firmware and software signing.
Acronym: LMS
Category: algorithm

GL:logical-qubit.full:
A fault-tolerant unit of quantum information built from many physical qubits combined via quantum error correction. Estimates of when a quantum computer could break RSA or ECC are expressed in logical qubits, not physical ones.
Category: concept

GL:lorawan.full:
Long Range Wide Area Network, a low-power WAN protocol for IoT. Uses AES-128 pre-shared keys. The maximum application payload of a frame depends on region and data rate: in the LoRaWAN 1.0.3 Regional Parameters it ranges from 11 bytes (US902-928, lowest data rate) to 242 bytes, and EU863-870 allows 51 to 222 bytes (242 without repeater compatibility). An ML-KEM-768 ciphertext alone is 1,088 bytes, so a PQC key exchange cannot fit in one frame and would need fragmentation across frames or a different exchange design.
Category: protocol

GL:macsec.full:
IEEE 802.1AE Media Access Control Security, providing Layer 2 encryption for Ethernet frames. Used to secure LAN traffic between switches and endpoints.
Acronym: MACsec
Category: protocol

GL:mas.full:
Singapore's central bank and integrated financial regulator. Publishes Technology Risk Management Guidelines and circulars that cover cryptographic-control expectations for financial institutions.
Acronym: Monetary Authority of Singapore
Category: organization

GL:matter.full:
Smart home interoperability standard (formerly Project CHIP). Uses the CASE protocol with ECDSA P-256 for device attestation. PQC migration requires protocol specification update.
Category: protocol

GL:mayo.full:
A multivariate signature candidate in the NIST signature on-ramp. Produces very small signatures (~420 bytes at NIST Cat 1) with relatively small public keys, derived from the Oil-and-Vinegar trapdoor.
Category: algorithm

GL:mdl.full:
Mobile Driver's License, a digital credential stored on a smartphone conforming to ISO/IEC 18013-5. Uses mdoc format with cryptographic device binding.
Acronym: mDL
Category: concept

GL:mdoc.full:
Mobile Document, a CBOR-based verifiable credential format defined in ISO/IEC 18013-5. Uses Mobile Security Objects (MSO) for issuer-signed data integrity.
Category: concept

GL:measured-boot.full:
A boot integrity mechanism where each stage of the boot process measures (hashes) the next stage and extends the measurement into TPM PCRs. Unlike Secure Boot which enforces policy by blocking unsigned code, Measured Boot records what ran for later attestation.
Category: concept

GL:merkle-tree.full:
A binary tree of hash values where each leaf contains a hash of a data block and each internal node contains a hash of its children. The foundation of stateful hash-based signature schemes.
Category: concept

GL:merkle-tree-certificate.full:
A certificate format that replaces individual per-certificate digital signatures with a compact inclusion proof in a Merkle tree. A single CA signature on the tree root covers the entire batch, dramatically reducing TLS handshake sizes for post-quantum algorithms.
Acronym: MTC
Category: concept

GL:merkle-tree-certificate-authority.full:
A Certificate Authority that collects certificate assertions into a Merkle tree, signs the root hash, and distributes inclusion proofs to subscribers. The MTCA replaces individual certificate signatures with batch-level tree signing.
Acronym: MTCA
Category: concept

GL:messaging-layer-security.full:
IETF group-messaging protocol (RFC 9420, July 2023) that scales end-to-end encryption to large groups using TreeKEM. Products implement it in different versions and modes; confirm support and scope in each vendor's own documentation before relying on it.
Acronym: MLS
Category: protocol

GL:micro-segmentation.full:
A network security technique that creates fine-grained security zones within a data centre, isolating individual workloads or applications from each other. Limits blast radius when an attacker gains access to one segment.
Category: concept

GL:middlebox-compatibility.full:
The ability of network intermediary devices (firewalls, load balancers, DPI appliances, TLS inspection proxies) to correctly process PQC-sized TLS handshakes and certificates without dropping, truncating, or rejecting connections due to unexpected packet sizes.
Category: concept

GL:milenage.full:
The set of cryptographic functions (f1–f5) used in 5G authentication. Based on AES and generates authentication vectors.
Category: concept

GL:min-entropy.full:
The most conservative measure of entropy, defined as the negative base-2 logarithm of the probability of the most likely outcome. Used by NIST SP 800-90B for entropy source validation.
Category: concept

GL:mitre.full:
A U.S. nonprofit operating federally funded R&D centers, best known in security circles for maintaining the CVE program and the ATT&CK adversary-tactics framework.
Acronym: MITRE
Category: organization

GL:ml-dsa.full:
Module-Lattice-Based Digital Signature Algorithm, the NIST-standardized PQC algorithm for digital signatures (formerly Dilithium). Defined in FIPS 204.
Category: algorithm

GL:ml-kem.full:
Module-Lattice-Based Key Encapsulation Mechanism, the NIST-standardized PQC algorithm for key exchange (formerly Kyber). Defined in FIPS 203.
Category: algorithm

GL:ml-kem-768.full: Post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism standardized in FIPS 203.

GL:model-collapse.full:
A degenerative process where AI models trained on AI-generated data progressively lose quality, diversity, and accuracy over successive generations, eventually producing incoherent or repetitive outputs.
Category: concept

GL:model-provenance.full:
The complete documented history of an AI model's creation — including training data sources, hyperparameters, training infrastructure, fine-tuning steps, and evaluation results — cryptographically signed to ensure integrity.
Category: concept

GL:model-weights.full:
The learned numerical parameters of a neural network that encode the model's knowledge. For large language models, weights can number in the hundreds of billions and represent millions of dollars in compute investment.
Category: concept

GL:modules-in-process-list.full:
The CMVP list of cryptographic modules on which the CMVP is actively working. For each submission it shows the module name, vendor name, standard and status together with the date the module went into that status. Because validation is a joint effort of the CMVP, the laboratory and the vendor, the list gives some indication of which of them has the action. Participation is voluntary, the list does not necessarily include all modules being tested or reviewed, and posting on it does not imply or guarantee FIPS 140 validation.
Acronym: MIP
Category: concept

GL:mpc-in-the-head.full:
A signature design that proves knowledge of a secret by simulating what a multi-party computation would output, then revealing just enough of the simulation to be verifiable. Used by FAEST (AES-based), MQOM (multivariate quadratic), and SDitH (syndrome decoding).
Acronym: MPCitH
Category: concept

GL:mqom.full:
An MPC-in-the-Head signature candidate in the NIST on-ramp whose security reduces to the hardness of solving systems of multivariate quadratic equations.
Acronym: Multivariate Quadratic on MPC-in-the-Head
Category: algorithm

GL:mqtt.full:
Message Queuing Telemetry Transport, a lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol for IoT. MQTT 5.0 supports TLS 1.3 transport security.
Acronym: MQTT
Category: protocol

GL:msin.full: Mobile Subscriber Identification Number — the portion of the IMSI that is concealed.

GL:msit-korea.full:
South Korea's policy ministry for science, ICT, and broadcasting. Co-sponsors the KpqC standardization competition with KISA and the National Intelligence Service.
Acronym: Ministry of Science and ICT
Category: organization

GL:mso-mdoc.full:
The CBOR-encoded mobile document credential format defined by ISO/IEC 18013-5, carrying a Mobile Security Object signed as a COSE_Sign1 structure. Optimised for proximity presentation over NFC or BLE.
Category: concept

GL:mtls.full:
Mutual TLS, a TLS mode where both client and server present certificates for authentication. Common in microservices, zero-trust architectures, and API security.
Category: protocol

GL:multivariate-cryptography.full:
PQC algorithms based on the hardness of solving systems of multivariate polynomial equations (usually quadratic) over a finite field. Produces tiny signatures and large public keys. Candidates include UOV, MAYO, QR-UOV, SNOVA.
Category: concept

GL:nb-iot.full:
Narrowband IoT, a cellular connectivity standard for low-power wide-area (LPWA) devices. Offers 62.5 kbps uplink bandwidth, making PQC handshake overhead a significant concern.
Acronym: NB-IoT
Category: protocol

GL:nccoe.full:
NIST National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence, collaborating with industry to develop practical PQC migration guidance and reference architectures.
Acronym: NCCoE
Category: organization

GL:ncsc.full:
UK National Cyber Security Centre, publishing PQC migration guidance and a 2035 deadline for full transition to quantum-safe cryptography.
Acronym: NCSC
Category: organization

GL:nerc-cip.full:
North American Electric Reliability Corporation Critical Infrastructure Protection standards. Mandatory cybersecurity requirements for bulk electric system operators.
Acronym: NERC CIP
Category: standard

GL:ngfw.full:
Next-Generation Firewall — a stateful network firewall that integrates application-layer inspection, user identity awareness, TLS inspection, IDS/IPS, and threat intelligence. Replaces traditional port-based packet filters with application-aware policies.
Acronym: NGFW
Category: concept

GL:niap.full:
National Information Assurance Partnership, the U.S. Common Criteria certification body operated jointly by NSA and NIST; issues CC certificates recognized under the CCRA (both already in this glossary).
Acronym: NIAP
Category: organization

GL:nis2.full:
EU directive (2022/2555) requiring enhanced cybersecurity controls across critical-infrastructure sectors. Transposition deadline October 2024; enforcement ongoing across member states. Mandates appropriate cryptographic measures without naming PQC explicitly.
Acronym: Network and Information Security Directive 2
Category: standard

GL:nis2-directive.full:
The EU Network and Information Security Directive 2 (Directive (EU) 2022/2555). Article 21 requires essential and important entities to take appropriate and proportionate cybersecurity risk-management measures, including policies and procedures on the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption. Member States had to adopt national measures by 17 October 2024 and apply them from 18 October 2024; what applies to a given entity depends on national law.
Category: standard

GL:nist.full:
National Institute of Standards and Technology, the U.S. agency leading PQC standardization through its Post-Quantum Cryptography project.
Acronym: NIST
Category: organization

GL:nist-ir-8105.full:
Report on Post-Quantum Cryptography (April 2016) — NIST's original report announcing the PQC standardization project and surveying the state of quantum-resistant cryptography at the time.
Category: standard

GL:nist-ir-8309.full:
Status Report on the Second Round of the NIST PQC Standardization Process (July 2020), narrowing the KEM and signature candidates to the finalists and alternates that became ML-KEM, ML-DSA, FN-DSA, and SLH-DSA.
Category: standard

GL:nist-ir-8413.full:
Status Report on the Third Round of the NIST PQC Standardization Process (July 2022), announcing the selection of ML-KEM, ML-DSA, and FN-DSA for standardization and continued fourth-round evaluation of alternate KEMs (BIKE, Classic McEliece, HQC, SIKE).
Category: standard

GL:nist-ir-8528.full:
NIST Internal Report (October 2024) that down-selected the PQC signature on-ramp to 14 second-round candidates across four mathematical families: MPC-in-the-Head, multivariate, isogeny, and lattice. Superseded by NIST IR 8610 (May 2026), which closed the second round and advanced nine candidates to the third round.
Category: standard

GL:nist-ir-8545.full:
NIST Internal Report documenting the selection of HQC as an additional KEM standard, providing a code-based alternative to lattice-based ML-KEM.
Category: standard

GL:nist-ir-8547.full:
NIST Internal Report setting the PQC transition timeline: quantum-vulnerable public-key algorithms are deprecated after 2030 and disallowed under NIST standards after 2035. Final since 27 October 2026; it replaced the initial public draft of 12 November 2024.
Category: standard

GL:nist-rmf.full:
NIST Risk Management Framework (SP 800-37 Rev. 2) — a seven-step lifecycle process (Prepare, Categorise, Select, Implement, Assess, Authorise, Monitor) for managing information security and privacy risk in information systems and organisations.
Acronym: RMF
Category: standard

GL:nist-sp-800-131a.full:
NIST Special Publication providing guidance on transitioning the use of cryptographic algorithms and key lengths. Defines which algorithms are approved, deprecated, or disallowed for federal use.
Category: standard

GL:nist-sp-800-186.full:
Recommendation for Discrete Logarithm-based Cryptography: Elliptic Curve Domain Parameters — the NIST standard specifying the NIST curves (P-256, P-384, P-521) used throughout TLS, X.509, and other classical or hybrid cryptography.
Category: standard

GL:nist-sp-800-208.full:
NIST recommendation for stateful hash-based signature schemes LMS and XMSS, used for firmware signing and secure boot.
Category: standard

GL:nist-sp-800-227.full:
NIST Special Publication providing recommendations for Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM) implementation, including guidance on parameter selection and secure use of ML-KEM.
Category: standard

GL:nist-sp-800-56a.full:
Recommendation for Pair-Wise Key-Establishment Using Discrete Logarithm Cryptography — the NIST standard specifying Diffie-Hellman and elliptic-curve (ECDH) key-agreement schemes.
Category: standard

GL:nist-sp-800-56b.full:
Recommendation for Pair-Wise Key-Establishment Using Integer Factorization Cryptography — the NIST standard specifying RSA-based key-transport and key-agreement schemes.
Category: standard

GL:nist-sp-800-56c.full:
Recommendation for Key-Derivation Methods in Key-Establishment Schemes — the NIST standard specifying the two-step (extract-then-expand) key-derivation approach used to turn a shared secret from SP 800-56A/B, or a PQC KEM, into usable keying material.
Category: standard

GL:nist-sp-800-57.full:
NIST Special Publication 800-57: Recommendation for Key Management. Part 1 Rev. 5 (May 2020) describes four key-management phases (pre-operational, operational, post-operational and destroyed), the key states within them, and cryptoperiod guidance. Revision 6 is an initial public draft (December 2025).
Category: standard

GL:no-cloning-theorem.full:
A fundamental quantum mechanics result proving it is impossible to create an identical copy of an unknown quantum state, providing the theoretical basis for QKD security.
Category: concept

GL:non-repudiation.full:
A digital signature gives evidence of origin and integrity. Non-repudiation is a legal and process outcome that also needs control of the signing key, identity binding, trusted time and policy; a valid signature alone cannot stop a signer from claiming key compromise. Relevant for legal documents, contracts, and financial transactions.
Category: concept

GL:nonce.full:
A random cryptographic value (typically 32 bytes) sent by the Initiator (Ni) or Responder (Nr) to prevent replay attacks and contribute to key derivation.
Acronym: Ni
Category: concept

GL:notation.full:
A CNCF OCI artifact signing tool that supports any OCI artifact (images, Helm charts, SBOMs) using X.509 certificate-backed signatures. We found no vendor documentation stating that Notation, or its AWS Signer plugin, supports ML-DSA, so any post-quantum support is unconfirmed.
Category: concept

GL:nsa.full:
National Security Agency, the U.S. intelligence agency that publishes CNSA 2.0 and mandates PQC adoption timelines for national security systems.
Acronym: NSA
Category: organization

GL:nsm-10.full:
National Security Memorandum on Promoting United States Leadership in Quantum Computing While Mitigating Risks to Vulnerable Cryptographic Systems, signed May 4, 2022. Directs NSA, CISA, and NIST to inventory cryptographic systems and sets migration timelines for National Security Systems.
Category: standard

GL:ntru.full:
A lattice-based key encapsulation mechanism built on the NTRU problem, one of the oldest practical lattice cryptosystems (1996) and a NIST PQC Round 3 finalist; not selected as ML-KEM (Kyber) became the primary standardized lattice KEM.
Category: algorithm

GL:ntru-lattice.full:
A lattice-based cryptographic family using polynomial rings, providing the mathematical basis for FN-DSA (Falcon). One of the earliest PQC proposals (1996).
Acronym: NTRU
Category: concept

GL:oasis.full:
Organization for the Advancement of Structured Information Standards, a nonprofit consortium that develops open standards — including KMIP, already in this glossary, which now extends to PQC key types.
Acronym: OASIS
Category: organization

GL:oauth.full:
An authorization framework (RFC 6749) that lets an application obtain limited access to a resource on a user's behalf via short-lived tokens, without handling the user's credentials directly.
Acronym: OAuth 2.0
Category: protocol

GL:ocsp.full:
Online Certificate Status Protocol, used to check whether an X.509 certificate has been revoked. An alternative to Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs).
Acronym: OCSP
Category: protocol

GL:oidc.full:
OpenID Connect — an identity layer built on top of OAuth 2.0 that allows clients to verify user identity based on authentication performed by an authorization server. Issues ID tokens (JWTs) containing user identity claims.
Acronym: OIDC
Category: concept

GL:omb.full:
Office of Management and Budget, the U.S. executive-branch office that issues implementation guidance directing federal agencies on PQC migration planning and budgeting.
Acronym: OMB
Category: organization

GL:omb-m-23-02.full:
US Office of Management and Budget memorandum (November 2022) directing federal agencies to submit an annual prioritized inventory of quantum-vulnerable cryptographic systems (excluding national security systems) until 2035 or as superseding guidance directs, plus an assessment of the funding needed to migrate them.
Category: standard

GL:one-time-signature.full:
A signature scheme where each private key must be used to sign exactly one message. Reusing a key leaks information that allows signature forgery.
Acronym: OTS
Category: concept

GL:opa-open-policy-agent.full:
A general-purpose policy engine that evaluates decisions against a defined policy (written in Rego). In Kubernetes, OPA Gatekeeper uses ConstraintTemplates to block admission of resources with quantum-vulnerable algorithm identifiers in cert-manager Certificate or Deployment resources.
Category: concept

GL:openid-connect.full:
An identity layer built on OAuth 2.0 that provides authentication via ID tokens (JWTs). Widely used for single sign-on across web and mobile applications.
Acronym: OIDC
Category: protocol

GL:openid4vci.full:
OpenID for Verifiable Credential Issuance, a protocol for issuing digital credentials to wallets.
Category: protocol

GL:openid4vp.full:
OpenID for Verifiable Presentations, a protocol for presenting digital credentials from a wallet to a verifier.
Category: protocol

GL:openpgp.full:
An open standard for email encryption and signing based on PGP. PQC integration adds composite ML-KEM+ECC encryption and ML-DSA+ECC signatures.
Category: protocol

GL:openssl.full:
The most widely deployed open-source cryptography and TLS toolkit, providing both a command-line tool and the libssl/libcrypto libraries that a large share of Linux, network appliance, and application-layer software links against for TLS and general cryptographic operations.
Category: concept

GL:openssl-provider.full:
A dynamically loadable module that extends OpenSSL with additional cryptographic algorithm implementations. In OpenSSL 3.x, all algorithm implementations are providers — the default provider supplies standard algorithms, and third-party providers (like oqsprovider) add PQC algorithms.
Category: concept

GL:oqs.full:
Open Quantum Safe, an open-source project providing C library (liboqs) implementations of post-quantum algorithms and integrations with OpenSSL, BoringSSL, and other libraries.
Acronym: OQS
Category: organization

GL:oqsprovider.full:
An OpenSSL 3.x provider plugin from the Open Quantum Safe project that adds post-quantum and hybrid algorithms from the liboqs library, mainly for testing and experimentation. OpenSSL applications can use them once the provider is loaded and the application or OpenSSL configuration asks for the algorithm.
Category: concept

GL:origin-shielding.full:
A CDN architecture pattern where a designated intermediate cache layer sits between edge PoPs and the origin server, reducing direct origin requests by concentrating them at that layer.
Category: concept

GL:oscca.full:
China's Office of State Commercial Cryptography Administration, managing China's independent cryptographic standards including SM2 and PQC competitions.
Acronym: OSCCA
Category: organization

GL:ota-updates.full:
Over-the-Air updates, the process of remotely delivering firmware or software to devices. Signature verification must be quantum-safe to prevent forgery.
Acronym: OTA
Category: concept

GL:owasp.full:
Open Worldwide Application Security Project, a nonprofit foundation producing widely used application-security guidance (e.g. the OWASP Top 10) that is beginning to address crypto-agility and PQC migration risk for software developers.
Acronym: OWASP
Category: organization

GL:p-256.full:
A NIST standard elliptic curve (also called secp256r1 or prime256v1) widely used in TLS, FIDO2, and government systems. Quantum-vulnerable.
Category: algorithm

GL:p-256-pkcs11.full: NIST prime256v1 (secp256r1) elliptic curve; 65-byte uncompressed points.

GL:p-384.full:
A NIST standard elliptic curve (secp384r1) offering 192-bit security. Used in high-security TLS configurations and government systems. Quantum-vulnerable.
Category: algorithm

GL:p2pkh.full:
Pay-to-Public-Key-Hash, a Bitcoin address format (starting with "1") that hides the public key behind a hash until the first spending transaction.
Category: concept

GL:pairwise-consistency-test.full:
A conditional self-test that a cryptographic module must perform on every public and private key pair it generates; the Implementation Guidance treats it as separate from a cryptographic algorithm self-test. For ML-KEM key pairs it consists of encapsulating a shared secret with the encapsulation key and decapsulating the result with the decapsulation key, and it passes if the two shared secrets are equal. It is not required when a key or key pair is imported from outside the module's cryptographic boundary.
Acronym: PCT
Category: concept

GL:pan.full:
Primary Account Number. The 16-19 digit card number on a payment card, used to identify the cardholder account.
Acronym: PAN
Category: concept

GL:passive-discovery.full:
A network analysis technique that inspects encrypted traffic in-flight without injecting any packets. Used to detect and classify cryptographic algorithms across TLS, SSH, IKEv2, and OT protocols by analyzing observable handshake metadata on a SPAN port or network tap.
Category: concept

GL:pbkdf2.full:
Password-Based Key Derivation Function 2, used to derive cryptographic keys from passwords. Applies a pseudorandom function (typically HMAC-SHA) iteratively.
Category: algorithm

GL:pci-dss.full:
Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard, requiring strong cryptography for cardholder data protection. Quantum threatens its RSA/ECC foundations.
Acronym: PCI DSS
Category: standard

GL:pci-ssc.full:
PCI Security Standards Council, the payment-card-industry body (founded by the major card brands) that maintains PCI DSS and is issuing PQC migration guidance for payments.
Acronym: PCI SSC
Category: organization

GL:pdpa.full:
Personal Data Protection Act — Singapore's primary data protection law administered by the PDPC. Section 24 requires organisations to make reasonable security arrangements to protect personal data in their possession or under their control. The PDPC's guidelines say there is no one-size-fits-all solution and list encrypting personal data among example technical measures.
Acronym: PDPA
Category: standard

GL:pem.full:
Privacy Enhanced Mail, a Base64-encoded format for storing cryptographic objects (certificates, keys, CSRs). Recognized by "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----" headers.
Acronym: PEM
Category: concept

GL:performance-baseline.full:
A set of established metrics for classical cryptographic algorithm performance (ECDH, RSA, ECDSA) used as a reference point to measure the overhead introduced by PQC algorithms. Enables data-driven decisions about hardware capacity, latency budgets, and migration sequencing.
Category: concept

GL:performance-budget.full:
The allocation of computational resources (CPU cycles, memory, bandwidth, latency) for cryptographic operations within an application or system. PQC algorithms have different performance profiles than classical algorithms, requiring budget redesign during migration.
Category: concept

GL:person-identification-data.full:
The digital identity credential in the EUDI Wallet ecosystem, containing core attributes like name, date of birth, and nationality issued by a national authority.
Acronym: PID
Category: concept

GL:physical-qubit.full:
A single physical two-level quantum system (e.g. a trapped ion, superconducting circuit, or photon) used as a qubit before error correction. Many physical qubits — current estimates range from hundreds to well over a thousand, depending on the error-correction code — are needed to form one reliable logical qubit.
Category: concept

GL:picnic.full:
A signature scheme built from symmetric primitives and zero-knowledge proofs rather than a hard math problem; a NIST PQC Round 3 alternate candidate not standardized, mainly due to large signature sizes and slow performance relative to SLH-DSA and ML-DSA.
Category: algorithm

GL:pipl.full:
Personal Information Protection Law — China's primary data privacy law (effective November 2021), requiring data processors to adopt security measures protecting personal information. Mandates localisation of certain data and restricts cross-border transfers, making PQC migration relevant for multinational organisations with Chinese data subjects.
Acronym: PIPL
Category: standard

GL:pkcs-1.full:
The RSA Cryptography Standard, specifying RSA encryption and signature padding schemes (PKCS#1 v1.5, OAEP, PSS) used across TLS, S/MIME, and code signing.
Category: standard

GL:pkcs-11.full:
A standard API (also called Cryptoki) for accessing cryptographic hardware like Hardware Security Modules (HSMs), smart cards, and tokens.
Category: standard

GL:pkcs-12.full:
A file format for storing a private key together with its X.509 certificate, commonly used for importing/exporting credentials.
Category: standard

GL:pkcs-7.full:
The Cryptographic Message Syntax standard for signing and encrypting arbitrary data, superseded by and largely synonymous with IETF CMS — the basis for S/MIME and code-signing signature formats.
Category: standard

GL:pkcs-8.full:
The standard syntax for encoding a private key, optionally password-encrypted, independent of its algorithm — the format OpenSSL's genpkey produces for RSA, ECDSA, and PQC key types alike.
Category: standard

GL:pki.full:
Framework of policies, processes, and components that issues, distributes, validates, and revokes digital certificates. PQC migration of PKI requires new certificate, CRL/OCSP, and timestamp signature algorithms (e.g. ML-DSA).
Acronym: Public Key Infrastructure
Category: concept

GL:platform-configuration-register.full:
A TPM register that accumulates integrity measurements (hash chains) of platform state: firmware, boot loader, kernel, and optionally application code. TPM2_Quote signs PCR values with the AIK to produce a verifiable attestation report.
Acronym: PCR
Category: concept

GL:platform-key.full:
The root of trust in UEFI Secure Boot: a single key whose private half the platform owner uses to change platform ownership and to authorise changes to the Key Exchange Key (KEK) list. The platform vendor can supply a default Platform Key, and the platform owner enrolls their own.
Acronym: PK
Category: concept

GL:post-quantum-cryptography.full:
Cryptographic algorithms designed to be secure against attacks by both classical and quantum computers.
Acronym: PQC
Category: concept

GL:pq3.full:
Apple's post-quantum protocol for iMessage, using a Kyber-based post-quantum key establishment with periodic re-keying. Apple's "Level 3" is Apple's own security-level scale for messaging, not a NIST security category.
Category: protocol

GL:pqc-migration-budget.full:
The estimated total cost of transitioning an organization's cryptographic infrastructure to post-quantum algorithms, including hardware upgrades, software updates, staff training, compliance certification, and operational overhead during the hybrid transition period.
Category: concept

GL:pqc-migration-priority.full:
A ranked ordering of data assets and cryptographic dependencies by urgency of migration to post-quantum algorithms. Priority is computed from sensitivity tier, HNDL risk window, regulatory obligations, and migration effort, enabling organisations to sequence their migration roadmap rationally.
Category: concept

GL:pqc-on-ramp.full:
NIST's ongoing process for additional post-quantum signature algorithms beyond the schemes it selected earlier (ML-DSA, SLH-DSA, FN-DSA). Progress is documented in NIST IR 8528 (first round, October 2024) and NIST IR 8610 (second round, May 2026); the aim is to diversify the signature portfolio, with particular interest in schemes that do not use structured lattices.
Category: concept

GL:pqca.full:
Post-Quantum Cryptographic Alliance, a Linux Foundation project bringing together industry and academia to advance PQC adoption through open-source software.
Acronym: PQCA
Category: organization

GL:pqclean.full:
A collection of clean, standalone C implementations of the post-quantum schemes in the NIST post-quantum project, written to be easy to integrate into libraries such as liboqs and the Rust pqcrypto crate. The project is retired and archived as read-only.
Category: concept

GL:pqxdh.full:
Post-Quantum Extended Diffie-Hellman, the key agreement Signal specified for adding post-quantum protection to session setup. It combines X25519 with a Kyber-1024 key encapsulation, the pre-standard predecessor of ML-KEM-1024. Support in other messengers must be confirmed from their own documentation.
Acronym: PQXDH
Category: protocol

GL:priority-date.full:
The earliest date an inventor can claim to have disclosed an invention, typically from an earlier-filed provisional or foreign application. It is the date patent examiners use to judge whether the claimed invention is novel against prior art.
Category: concept

GL:privacy-amplification.full:
A post-processing step in QKD that applies a randomly chosen two-universal hash function to the corrected key, shortening it so that an eavesdropper's remaining information is negligible, given an estimate of how much she could have learned.
Category: concept

GL:private-key.full:
A cryptographic key kept secret by its owner. Used to decrypt data or create digital signatures.
Category: concept

GL:programmable-logic-controller.full:
An industrial computer that controls manufacturing processes, assembly lines, and infrastructure equipment. PLCs sit at Purdue Level 1 and typically use pre-shared keys or DNP3-SA for authentication.
Acronym: PLC
Category: concept

GL:protection-profile.full:
In Common Criteria, an implementation-independent statement of security needs for a type of target of evaluation (TOE). It describes the TOE type and the security functional and assurance requirements expected of it, and is typically written where a user community, a regulator or a group of developers wants to define a common set of security needs. A Security Target for a specific product may conform to one or more Protection Profiles.
Acronym: PP
Category: concept

GL:provider-model.full:
A software architecture pattern that abstracts cryptographic operations behind an interchangeable provider interface, enabling algorithm substitution without changing application code. Examples: Java JCA/JCE providers, OpenSSL provider API (3.x), PKCS#11 as an HSM provider.
Category: concept

GL:psk.full:
In TLS 1.3, a symmetric key issued by the server after a full handshake and presented by the client on reconnection to enable session resumption — feeding into the Early Secret stage of a faster resumed handshake, optionally with 0-RTT early data.
Acronym: Pre-Shared Key
Category: protocol

GL:public-body-electronic-attestation-of.full:
An attestation issued by a public body on the basis of an authentic source.
Acronym: PuB-EAA
Category: concept

GL:public-key.full:
A cryptographic key that can be shared openly. Used to encrypt data or verify digital signatures.
Category: concept

GL:public-key-infrastructure.full:
The system of Certificate Authorities, digital certificates, and registration authorities that manages public keys and enables secure communication.
Acronym: PKI
Category: protocol

GL:purdue-model.full:
Reference architecture for industrial control system (ICS) networks. Defines 6 levels from physical process (Level 0) to enterprise network (Level 5), guiding security zone segmentation and PQC migration priority.
Category: concept

GL:q-day.full:
The hypothetical future date when a quantum computer becomes powerful enough to break current public-key cryptography (RSA, ECC).
Category: concept

GL:qber.full:
Quantum Bit Error Rate, the fraction of sifted key bits where Alice and Bob disagree despite using the same measurement basis. Eavesdropping raises it, but so do noise and device imperfections, so a high value is an alarm, not proof of an adversary.
Acronym: QBER
Category: concept

GL:qkd.full:
Quantum Key Distribution, a method of distributing encryption keys using quantum physics rather than mathematical hardness. Distinct from PQC and requires specialized hardware.
Acronym: QKD
Category: concept

GL:qrng.full:
Quantum Random Number Generator. A device that generates random numbers from quantum mechanical phenomena such as photon detection, vacuum fluctuations, or quantum beam splitting.
Acronym: QRNG
Category: concept

GL:qtsp.full:
Qualified Trust Service Provider, an organization authorized under eIDAS 2.0 to issue qualified electronic signatures, seals, timestamps, and certificates.
Acronym: QTSP
Category: concept

GL:qualified-electronic-attestation-of-a.full:
An attestation of attributes issued by a Qualified Trust Service Provider, carrying legal weight across all EU member states.
Acronym: QEAA
Category: concept

GL:qualified-electronic-signature.full:
A digital signature with the legal equivalence of a handwritten signature under EU law, requiring a qualified certificate and a secure creation device.
Acronym: QES
Category: concept

GL:quantum-advantage.full:
The point at which a quantum computer can solve a specific problem faster than any classical computer. Also called "quantum supremacy."
Category: concept

GL:quantum-computer.full:
A new type of computer that uses quantum physics. For certain specific problems it can be far faster than a standard computer, but it is not faster at everything.
Category: concept

GL:quantum-computing.full:
A type of computing that uses quantum-mechanical phenomena like superposition and entanglement to perform calculations exponentially faster than classical computers for certain problems.
Category: concept

GL:quantum-error-correction.full:
Techniques to protect quantum information from decoherence and errors during computation. Essential for building practical, large-scale quantum computers.
Category: concept

GL:quantum-risk-exposure.full:
A measure of an organization's vulnerability to quantum computing threats, combining data sensitivity, cryptographic algorithm usage, data retention periods, and the estimated timeline to a cryptographically relevant quantum computer (CRQC).
Category: concept

GL:quantum-safe-research-data.full:
Research datasets, publications, and intellectual property that require long-term confidentiality (20–50+ years) and integrity protection, making them particularly vulnerable to Harvest Now, Decrypt Later attacks and requiring early PQC adoption.
Category: concept

GL:quantum-supremacy.full:
A milestone at which a quantum computer performs a specific computation infeasible for any classical computer in a practical time, regardless of whether that computation is useful.
Category: concept

GL:qubit.full:
The basic unit of quantum information, analogous to a classical bit but capable of existing in superposition of 0 and 1 simultaneously.
Category: concept

GL:queryable-encryption.full:
An encryption scheme that allows a database server to execute certain queries over encrypted data without decrypting it first. MongoDB's Queryable Encryption encrypts fields on the client and supports equality queries, and in newer releases range queries, over encrypted indexes. It is different from storage encryption such as TDE, which the server decrypts transparently.
Category: concept

GL:quic.full:
A modern transport protocol built on UDP, providing encrypted connections with lower latency than TCP+TLS. The foundation of HTTP/3.
Category: protocol

GL:raci-matrix.full:
A responsibility assignment matrix (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed) used in project governance to clarify roles and decision rights across stakeholders. Essential for cross-functional PQC migration programs.
Acronym: RACI
Category: concept

GL:rad-hardened-processor.full:
A microprocessor designed to operate in high-radiation environments (space, nuclear facilities) with protection against single-event effects, total ionizing dose, and latch-up.
Category: concept

GL:rainbow.full:
A multivariate-quadratic digital signature scheme and NIST PQC Round 3 finalist, eliminated in 2022 after a rank-based cryptanalysis attack recovered a Rainbow private key on a single laptop in about a weekend.
Category: algorithm

GL:registration-authority.full:
The entity in a PKI that verifies a certificate applicant's identity and authorizes issuance, then forwards the approved request to the Certificate Authority (already in this glossary) for signing.
Acronym: RA
Category: protocol

GL:rekor.full:
The transparency log component of Sigstore. Rekor is an immutable, append-only log that records every signing event — signature, certificate, and artifact hash — for public auditability.
Category: concept

GL:related-certificate.full:
A certificate-binding mechanism in RFC 9763 for associating two independently issued end-entity X.509 certificates with the same entity. A new certificate can contain a RelatedCertificate extension identifying a related certificate by its digest and hash algorithm. For example, a new PQC certificate can reference an existing classical certificate while each retains its own key and signature.
Acronym: RFC 9763
Category: concept

GL:relying-party.full:
An entity (organization, service, or application) that relies on a digital credential presented by a holder to make trust decisions — such as granting access or completing a transaction.
Category: concept

GL:remote-attestation.full:
A protocol in which a platform (the attester) sends signed evidence about its measured state to a remote verifier, which appraises it against reference values and a policy and produces a result for a relying party to act on. It supports a trust decision; it does not prove the software is free of flaws. The signature scheme on the evidence depends on the platform; where it is ECDSA, it is quantum-vulnerable.
Category: concept

GL:remote-hsm.full:
A Hardware Security Module operated by a provider rather than held on the user's device. The EUDI ARF supports both local WSCD and remote WSCD (HSM) models.
Category: concept

GL:remote-terminal-unit.full:
A microprocessor-controlled device that interfaces field devices (sensors, actuators) to a SCADA system. RTUs sit at Purdue Level 1 with asset lifecycles of 15–25 years.
Acronym: RTU
Category: concept

GL:return-on-investment.full:
A financial metric comparing the benefit generated with the cost invested, usually (benefit − cost) ÷ cost over a stated period. For PQC migration the benefit is estimated from breach avoidance savings, compliance penalty avoidance and operational efficiency gains, and the cost is the migration investment. Net benefit (benefit minus cost) is a different quantity; the period, discounting and assumptions behind each benefit must be stated for the figure to mean anything.
Acronym: ROI
Category: concept

GL:reverse-proxy.full:
A server that sits between clients and origin servers, forwarding client requests and returning responses on behalf of the origin. It provides TLS termination, load balancing, caching, and security filtering.
Category: concept

GL:rfc-7228.full:
Terminology for Constrained-Node Networks. Defines device Class 0/1/2 based on RAM and Flash memory constraints, used to categorize IoT device capabilities for protocol selection.
Category: standard

GL:rfc-8391.full:
The IETF specification for XMSS (eXtended Merkle Signature Scheme) and XMSS^MT, the stateful hash-based signature schemes also standardized by NIST SP 800-208.
Category: standard

GL:rfc-8446.full:
The original IETF standard defining TLS version 1.3, published August 2018. TLS 1.3 removed legacy cipher suites, mandated forward secrecy, and reduced the handshake to 1 round-trip. Obsoleted by RFC 9846 (July 2026), which re-specifies TLS 1.3 under the same version number.
Category: standard

GL:rfc-8554.full:
The IETF specification for LMS (Leighton-Micali Signatures) and its multi-tree variant HSS, the stateful hash-based signature schemes also standardized by NIST SP 800-208.
Category: standard

GL:rfc-9370.full:
IETF standard defining multiple key exchanges in IKEv2, enabling hybrid classical + PQC key exchange for IPsec VPNs.
Category: standard

GL:rfc-9629.full:
IETF standard defining how to use Key Encapsulation Mechanisms (KEMs) in the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) for encrypted messaging.
Category: standard

GL:rfc-9794.full:
IETF Informational RFC (June 2025) that defines terminology for post-quantum/traditional (PQ/T) hybrid schemes, so that protocols, standards and organisations use the word "hybrid" consistently. It is a reference terminology guide and does not set protocol rules.
Category: protocol

GL:rfc-9881.full:
IETF standard defining how to use ML-DSA digital signatures in X.509 certificates and Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs).
Category: standard

GL:rfc-9882.full:
IETF standard defining the use of ML-DSA signatures in the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS), enabling PQC-signed messages and documents.
Category: standard

GL:ripemd-160.full:
A 160-bit cryptographic hash function used in Bitcoin address derivation (applied to the SHA-256 digest of a public key). Its 160-bit output gives about 80 bits of generic classical collision resistance, and an ideal Grover preimage search is about 2^80 queries before circuit costs; it is not a NIST-approved hash, and no blanket "quantum-safe" verdict follows from its output size.
Category: algorithm

GL:risk-heatmap.full:
A 5×5 grid visualisation plotting risks by likelihood (y-axis) and impact (x-axis). Cells are colour-coded green to red to indicate overall risk level. Used in PQC risk management to communicate prioritisation of quantum-vulnerable assets to executive stakeholders.
Category: concept

GL:risk-register.full:
A structured document that records identified risks, their likelihood, potential impact, current controls, and treatment decisions. For PQC, the risk register captures each quantum-vulnerable cryptographic asset, the HNDL exposure window, and the planned migration action with owner and deadline.
Category: concept

GL:risk-treatment.full:
The process of selecting and implementing options to address an identified risk. The four options are commonly summarised as Mitigate (implement controls), Accept (tolerate the risk), Transfer (insurance/outsource) and Avoid (cease the activity); ISO/IEC 27005 names them risk modification, risk retention, risk sharing and risk avoidance. For quantum risk, "Mitigate" means migrating to PQC; "Accept" is a documented decision made within the organisation's risk appetite and based on the data's confidentiality lifetime and exposure, and it does not undo any data an adversary has already captured.
Category: concept

GL:rlp.full:
Recursive Length Prefix, Ethereum's serialization encoding for transactions, blocks, and account state. Used to encode transaction data before signing with ECDSA.
Acronym: RLP
Category: concept

GL:root-ca.full:
The top-level Certificate Authority in a PKI trust hierarchy. A Root CA issues a self-signed certificate that serves as the trust anchor — all certificates in the chain ultimately derive their trust from it.
Category: concept

GL:root-of-trust.full:
A foundational component (hardware or software) that is inherently trusted and used as the starting point for a chain of trust in a system.
Category: concept

GL:rosenpass.full:
A post-quantum key exchange protocol designed as a companion to WireGuard VPN. Performs a separate key exchange using Classic McEliece and the pre-standard round-3 Kyber-512 (not FIPS 203 ML-KEM) and feeds the resulting key into WireGuard.
Category: protocol

GL:rsa.full:
A widely used classical public-key algorithm based on the difficulty of factoring large numbers. Vulnerable to quantum attacks via Shor's algorithm.
Category: algorithm

GL:rustcrypto.full:
A community-maintained collection of cryptographic algorithm implementations in Rust, published as modular crates on crates.io. Emphasizes type safety, zero-dependency design, and no_std compatibility.
Category: concept

GL:s-mime.full:
Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions, a standard for email encryption and digital signing. PQC integration via ML-KEM and ML-DSA.
Acronym: S/MIME
Category: protocol

GL:saber.full:
A module-lattice-based key encapsulation mechanism and NIST PQC Round 3 finalist alongside Kyber and NTRU; not selected because NIST judged Kyber (now ML-KEM) the stronger overall combination of security and performance among the lattice KEMs.
Category: algorithm

GL:saml-2-0.full:
Security Assertion Markup Language 2.0 — an XML-based open standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between identity providers and service providers. The dominant enterprise SSO federation protocol.
Acronym: SAML
Category: concept

GL:sase.full:
Secure Access Service Edge — a cloud-delivered architecture combining network security functions (SWG, CASB, ZTNA, FWaaS) with WAN capabilities, delivered as a unified service at the network edge.
Acronym: SASE
Category: concept

GL:sbom.full:
Software Bill of Materials, a formal record of the components in a software product and their supply-chain relationships. Increasingly required alongside CBOM for security compliance.
Acronym: SBOM
Category: concept

GL:scada.full:
Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition, industrial control systems used in power grids, water treatment, and manufacturing. Quantum-vulnerable via legacy crypto.
Acronym: SCADA
Category: concept

GL:schannel.full:
Microsoft's Secure Channel cryptographic package — the TLS/SSL implementation built into Windows. SChannel is used by IIS, WinHTTP, and most Windows network services. It uses CNG (Cryptography API: Next Generation) for algorithm implementations.
Category: concept

GL:sct.full:
Signed Certificate Timestamp — a cryptographic proof from a Certificate Transparency log server that a certificate has been submitted and will be publicly logged. Required by Chrome for all TLS certificates since 2018.
Acronym: SCT
Category: concept

GL:sd-jwt.full:
Selective Disclosure JSON Web Token, a credential format that allows holders to reveal only specific claims from a signed token without exposing all data.
Acronym: SD-JWT
Category: concept

GL:sd-jwt-vc.full:
The Selective Disclosure JWT Verifiable Credential profile (draft-ietf-oauth-sd-jwt-vc), built on base SD-JWT (RFC 9901). Uses the dc+sd-jwt media type, which replaced vc+sd-jwt in November 2024.
Category: concept

GL:sda.full:
Static Data Authentication. The simplest EMV card authentication method where the issuer pre-signs static card data with RSA. Vulnerable to card cloning since the signature never changes.
Acronym: SDA
Category: protocol

GL:sdith.full:
An MPC-in-the-Head signature candidate in the NIST on-ramp whose security reduces to the hardness of syndrome decoding (the same combinatorial problem underlying code-based KEMs).
Acronym: Syndrome Decoding in the Head
Category: algorithm

GL:sealing-key.full:
